articles.author: Vincent O’Neill
articles.summary: A Libertarian plan to balance the federal budget in one year through spending cuts, eliminating agencies, ending foreign aid and military compensation payments, and repaying debts.

body.text: Although President Trump and his friend Elon Musk have made a good start in regard to reducing the size of the federal workforce, they have a long way to go as far as reducing the national budget is concerned. This is due to the fact that they require the assistance of the Republican and Democrat parties, who are a combination of clueless and irresponsible.

The 2024 deficit for the national government was $1.832.86 trillion. The deficit for the first 5 months of fiscal year 2025 (October-February) was a record $1.147 trillion. The projected deficit for the year is over $3.4 trillion.

The only response from the Republicans and Democrats was to pass another “temporary spending bill to fund the government for another 6 months.” Their bill will cut national government spending by $7 billion dollars, which would be a cut of 0.103% from the previous year, unless the increase in interest on the national debt is included. When interest on the national debt is included ($952 billion in 2024, over $1 trillion in 2025), their bill is a spending increase.

Since that is not acceptable, the following is a Libertarian alternative. The achievable goal is for a balanced national budget or yearly surplus in ONE YEAR. The maximum time for this is to occur is 6 years or less. A drastic reduction of economic interventionism occurs as the national budget is sharply reduced.

“Moreover, a drastic cut in the government budget--both in taxes and expenditures--will of itself speed adjustment by changing the social choice toward more saving and investment relative to consumption. For government spending, whatever the label attached to it, is solely consumption. Any cut in the budget, therefore, raises the investment-consumption ratio in the economy and allows more rapid validation of originally wasteful and loss-yielding projects.” - Murray Rothbard, “America’s Great Depression”, p.167
The Congressional Budget Office stated the budget expense was $6.2 trillion for 2023, $6.8 trillion in 2024.

body.text: Returning to a constitutionally limited and non-interventionist foreign policy will lead to a massive reduction in the bloated $800 billion plus military budget.

The foreign policy of the U.S. has been less than exemplary for quite a long time. We will start with the fact that the United States has bombed at least 32 countries without a preceding declaration of war since the end of World War II and go on from there.

Once this issue is addressed, the U.S. responsibility to restore constitutional foreign policy could then be addressed. The end of an interventionist foreign policy will be one result. It will also create a foundation where the end of economic interventionism will follow logically.
As long as a sincere effort is made to address this and related issues, the likelihood of a foundation for World Peace being created increases exponentially.

The outline for this is shown in the previous articles “Creation of a Foundation for Middle East Peace” (August 2024 issue of Free New York) and “U.S. Foreign Policy and World Peace” (October 2024 issue of Free New York), and the procedure is described below in #6. “Military Budget Reduction/Compensation to be paid.”
Plan on a Steady and Continuing Yearly Military Budget Reduction.
The first year target is $100 Billion.

Its first budget in fiscal year 2021 was $15.3 billion, and it grew to $18 billion in 2022. It jumped to $26.3 billion in 2023 due to internal funds transfers from the Space Development Agency and the Air Force, plus a congressional add-on. Mar 13, 2023.
Their proposed budget is $30 billion for 2024.
Privatize NASA. Their 2023 budget was $25.4 billion, a 5.6% increase over the previous year.

They also have many assets to sell.
$3.263.17 Trillion+$30 Billion+$32.41 Billion=$3.325.58 Trillion Cut to this point.
3. Eliminating, Unconstitutional, Redundant and/or Stupid National Government Agencies

The total amount to be eliminated is unknown, but it is substantial. The national government currently contains 440 agencies and 2 million employees. The following is an improvement on the procedure being utilized by President Trump and his friend Elon Musk.

All national government agencies will be reviewed, all that are unconstitutional and/or counterproductive will be eliminated or phased out at the national level. This means that most national government agencies will be eliminated over time.
Not only is the yearly budget expense eliminated, but also all the unnecessary costs they place on honest Americans.

This will be done with minimal disruption to the labor market in the following manner. In the year that an agency is eliminated, all the current employees will receive their full salary, whether or not they get a different job.
So in the first year the agency is eliminated except for the cost of salaries, in the second year the cost is reduced to zero.

The real purpose of the NHTSA, like many government agencies, is to mandate optional, expensive and unnecessary items. (The mandatory “Safety Measure” Air bags are an example.

“From 1996 to 2000, 191 people, including 116 children, died in cases in which an air bag was or was suspected to be the cause. In many cases, the deaths came in low-speed crashes, in which the force of the deploying air bags proved fatal.” NewYork Times, Aug. 30, 2001

Automakers always comply, since they not only pass on the cost, the price becomes INFINITY once it is mandated. An incredible markup is permitted. A market with a price level of infinity is not a competitive market. NHTSA does this all the time.
Eliminate the NHTSA and massive savings for consumers will occur, safety enhanced, and a tremendous competitive market will ensue.

5. A Small Move Toward a Gold Standard and Sound Currency

Each year the national government will take 1% of tax revenue and purchase gold. The gold must be held for at least 3 years, so this will not be a mere book-keeping transaction. State and local governments should also do this.
Additionally, 1/10 of 1 percent will be used to buy silver. The country will therefore be making a small move toward a gold and silver standard.
This is tied in with the progression for eliminating the income tax.
Compensation will be deducted from the military budget and paid to foreign governments for four foreign policy crimes:

• Bombing a foreign country without a preceding Declaration of War • Attempting or succeeding in overthrowing the government of a foreign country without a preceding declaration of war • Placing economic sanctions on a foreign country without a preceding declaration of war • Any country that had toxins dropped on their country as part of an undeclared war would be entitled to compensation for this infraction.
This includes dropped pesticides, herbicides, etc. as was done as part of the “War on Drugs.”

Budgetary reduction will therefore occur through a modern adaptation of the Eric-fine for homicide.
The U.S will pay the Eric-fine once only per violation, and wipe the slate clean.

articles.title: Landlord Protection Law
articles.author: Rick Miller
articles.summary: An op-ed arguing that landlords and tenants, and companies and consumers, have equivalent motives, so neither side justifies government intervention.

body.text: Tenants and consumers seem to need protection from landlords and companies. Or is it that one-sided? Perhaps landlords and companies need protection. Some tenants are irresponsible and even dangerous. I have not always been an ideal tenant, to put it mildly. Consumers have been so greedy that they have driven companies to bankruptcy, as was the case several times with US automobile companies – except the government bailed them out each time, along with the powerful UAW union.

Landlords want the most rent they can get. How different are they from tenants? Tenants want the lowest possible rent. The motives of the two sides are exactly the same – neither has a claim to moral superiority. The same moral equivalence holds true with consumers and corporations.

So, why not have landlord and company protection laws instead of tenant and consumer protections? Just as logical, right? Which is to say neither one justifies government intervention on behalf of either side.

I hear one argument against what I have written; the difference in power between landlords and tenants and companies and consumers. It is usually the case that individual landlords are more powerful than individual tenants. However, as a group, tenants have as much power as landlords. The example I gave above about the automobile industry indicates the great power held by consumers; they can bankrupt industries.

articles.title: The Porcupine at 50 Years
articles.author: Andrew Kolstee
articles.summary: Fifty years after the Free Libertarian Party chose the porcupine as its animal at the 1975 convention, a look at how it happened.

body.cap: The original image of the porcupine used by the

body.text: When working on the history project for the Libertarian Party of New York, despite having the old newsletters, I was unaware of one major event that happened in the Libertarian Party of New York’s history that became a major part of the Libertarian Party—and that is the introduction of the porcupine as the party’s animal, which originaled in New York 50 years ago this month. John Caulfield related the story to me in 2021, and so that led me to dig deeper into the history of the famous symbol of the party.

The April/May 1975 Free Libertarian newsletter provided most of the written record of the events that unfolded on Sunday, April 6, 1975, the last day of the third annual convention of Libertarian Party of New York, known at that time as the Free Libertarian Party (FLP).
State Committee Member-At-Large (and the first elected chair of the LPNY) Andrea Millen wrote the following:

“Marty Nixon proposed we have a party animal and suggested the skunk. Someone amended the motion to make it “with tail raised.” Someone else proposed the rattlesnake and, of course some wiseguy amended to, “with tail raised.” Then someone else proposed the porcupine and naturally, it was amended to “with quills raised.” Certain that I had completely lost control of the entire Convention, I recognized Fran Youngstein to explain why we needed a party animal. With her usual perspicacity, Fran told us it was for “the annual football game between the FLP and SWP.” On the strength of that logic, the porcupine swept the field and I was finally able to gavel the convention back to order, just in time to adjourn.”
State Committee Member-At-Large Carolyn Keelan (who later served as Vice-Chair) wrote the following:

“Well, we did it, and here (s)he is – the Official FLP Animal – porcupine, with quills raised. And we picked well, thanks to Mickey Zweig’s excellent suggestion and exposition. Porcupines really are natural libertarians – unaggressive, good natured and incapable of being domesticated. If attacked, they first rattle their quills in warning, producing a sound similar to a rattlesnake. If the aggressor ignores the warning and continues to initiate force, porcupines turn their backs, erect their quills, and charge ass-backwards! (I told you they were libertarians.)

The fifteen-pound porcupine has killed mountain lions who wouldn’t heed that “Leave me alone!” warning! But (s)he never starts a fight – the old quill throwing legend is a calumny. The porcupine is even vegetarian, eating green vegetables, grains and bark. And (s)he’s surely the cutest party animal going – just look at the competition: a jackass, a buck-toothed rodent and a Durante-nosed mammal with weight problems.”

articles.title: RFK Jr Must Rescind EUA Amendment 12, Stop NY Adult Vaccine Mandate Bills
articles.author: Rich Purtell
articles.summary: An op-ed urging the rescinding of PREP Act EUA Amendment 12 and opposing New York bills that would require reporting adult vaccinations to the state.

body.text: Standing for Health Privacy and Accountability

In a time when public health and personal freedom intersect more than ever, the debate over the PREP Act EUA Amendment 12 and the proposed bills in New York State to mandate adult vaccination reporting into the state health department database has gained significant momentum.

The Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness (PREP) Act, enacted in 2005, grants immunity to certain individuals and entities against legal claims related to the manufacture, distribution, administration, and use of medical countermeasures during a public health emergency. Amendment 12 to the PREP Act Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) has extended these immunities for FIVE MORE YEARS UNTIL DECEMBER 2029 to include additional protections for manufacturers and healthcare providers, potentially limiting recourse for those adversely affected by vaccinations and treatments.

Rescinding the PREP Act EUA Amendment 12 is crucial to restore balance and accountability within the healthcare system. By providing sweeping immunity to manufacturers and healthcare providers, this amendment compromises the ability of individuals to seek justice and proper compensation for adverse effects. Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s action to rescind this amendment would demonstrate a commitment to transparency, accountability, and the protection of individual rights.
New York State’s Proposed Bills for Mandatory Vaccination Reporting

In parallel, New York State has introduced proposed legislation that would mandate the reporting of adult vaccinations into the state health department database. This legislative move raises significant concerns regarding privacy, consent, and the potential for misuse of personal health information.

Mandatory reporting of vaccinations encroaches upon the fundamental right to privacy and personal autonomy. The collection and centralization of personal health data can lead to unauthorized access and misuse, jeopardizing the confidentiality of medical records.
Advocates argue that individuals should have the right to control their personal health information and make informed decisions without government overreach.
The Importance of Legislative Advocacy and Public Action

To address these pressing issues, legislative advocacy and public action are paramount. Citizens must engage with their representatives, express their concerns, and demand legislative reforms that prioritize accountability, transparency, and personal freedom. By voicing our opinions and participating in public discourse, we can influence policy decisions and safeguard our rights.

The need for RFK Jr. to rescind the PREP Act EUA Amendment 12 and the proposed bills in New York State for mandatory vaccination reporting are critical issues that require immediate attention. As advocates for legislative change, it is our responsibility to remain informed, engaged, and proactive in defending our rights and ensuring that public health measures do not compromise individual freedoms. Together, we can work towards a balanced approach that upholds accountability, transparency, and the protection of personal privacy.

articles.title: Benefits of Splitting the Independent Nominating Petition Period in New York
articles.author: Rich Purtell
articles.summary: Argues that splitting the independent nominating petition into two parallel efforts would clarify candidates for voters and help minor parties.

body.text: The state of New York is considering a novel approach to the independent nominating petition period by splitting it into two distinct parallel efforts. The existing process, known as the “independent nominating petition,” will remain, focusing solely on the candidate’s name without any party affiliation. However, a new type, referred to as the “minor party nominating petition,” will be introduced, which will list both the candidate’s name and the minor party’s name. This minor party has the potential to become a constituted party in New York if it meets certain criteria in statewide elections for governor or president of the US.
There are several significant benefits to this proposed change, primarily centered on enhancing transparency for voters.
Clearer Distinction Between Candidate and Party

Splitting the petition process allows voters to differentiate clearly between candidates who are truly independent and those who are supported by minor parties. The “independent nominating petition” will ensure that candidates not affiliated with any party can present themselves purely on their individual merits and policies. Conversely, the “minor party nominating petition” will provide visibility to smaller parties, giving them a platform to promote their values and goals alongside their endorsed candidate.

With the new petition system, voters will have more information at their disposal. Knowing whether a candidate is running independently or with party backing helps voters make more informed decisions. This clarity can be particularly beneficial during local elections where party lines may not be as clearly defined as in larger, national contests.

The introduction of the “minor party nominating petition” offers an invaluable opportunity for smaller parties to gain traction and visibility. It provides a structured pathway for these parties to potentially achieve constituted party status in New York. This can lead to a more diverse political landscape, encouraging the emergence of new ideas and policies that may otherwise remain in the shadows.

Transparency in the nominating process can boost political engagement among voters. When the electoral process is clear and straightforward, voters feel more confident and motivated to participate. This engagement is crucial for a thriving democracy, ensuring that elected officials accurately represent the will of the people.

The benefits of splitting the independent nominating petition period in New York into two parallel efforts are manifold. By distinguishing between purely independent candidates and those affiliated with minor parties, voters gain greater clarity and information, promoting informed decision-making. Additionally, the proposal provides a platform for minor parties to grow and potentially achieve formal recognition, enriching the political landscape. Ultimately, this approach enhances transparency and promotes political engagement, strengthening the democratic process in New York.

articles.title: NY’s S227A: When Code Becomes Contraband and Freedom Gets a Timeout
articles.author: Christopher Skelly
articles.summary: Criticizes state bill S227A, which would criminalize sharing digital files for 3D-printed firearm parts and expand surveillance, as an attack on free speech and innovation.

body.text: New York State Senate Bill S227A, currently in committee, represents an overreach that threatens individual liberty, free expression, and personal sovereignty. If enacted, it would criminalize the sharing of digital files for 3D-printed firearm parts, expand surveillance, and impose restrictive licensing. This bill undermines the principles of innovation and open information, setting a dangerous precedent for state control.
Section 265.10(10) of S227A makes it a crime to share digital files—such as CAD or STL formats—with recipients who are not properly licensed.
Code is a form of speech, a means of communication and creation.

Criminalizing the sharing of digital files would impose prior restraint, punishing individuals for distributing information that has not caused harm. This is akin to censoring encryption tools or whistleblowers and chills open discourse in the name of safety.

S227A also amends Section 700.05 to permit wiretaps for suspected violations of this law, even without evidence of harm or intent. This lowers the threshold for state intrusion, eroding Fourth Amendment protections. The law’s Minority Report-style pre-crime approach assumes guilt based on potential, not action, threatening privacy rights.

By defining 3D printers as tools with criminal potential, S227A creates around the ownership of technology that could be used unlawfully—even if it hasn’t been. It targets the possibility of harm, not wrongdoing, effectively criminalizing innovation and the tools that enable it.

The bill also requires individuals to obtain both a New York gunsmith registration and a federal Type 7 FFL to legally receive such digital files. This creates a bureaucratic gatekeeping system that excludes hobbyists and innovators. This is not about safety—it is about control. Knowledge should be freely shared, not restricted by the state.

S227A punishes the sharing of digital files regardless of intent or actual harm. This creates a victimless crime statute that expands government authority over thought and communication. Its vague language also threatens open-source communities, where non-lethal designs could be misinterpreted as criminal.
This bill sets a chilling precedent for state control over digital information, undermining both freedom and innovation. It must be rejected.

articles.title: Onondaga Co. Libertarian Party Endorses Tom Babilon for Mayor of Syracuse
articles.author: Rose Leatherman
articles.role: State Committee Member (JD5), Onondaga County Secretary
articles.summary: The Onondaga County Libertarian Party endorses longtime member Tom Babilon, a lawyer, for the 2025 Syracuse mayoral election.

body.text: The Onondaga County Libertarian Party is proud to endorse longtime member and Syracuse city resident Tom Babilon for the 2025 mayoral election. Running on the Republican ticket, Babilon’s platform reflects core Libertarian principles of fiscal responsibility, property rights, and individual liberty.

Babilon’s campaign focuses on reducing the tax burden on residents, eliminating unnecessary regulations in order to foster small business growth, and finding more efficient approaches to city services. Committed to upholding the values of transparency and accountability in city governance, Babilon pledges to carefully review the city budget, reduce costs through consolidation of services, eliminate no-bid deals, and cut wasteful spending that fails to deliver results.

With 22 years of legal experience, Babilon served as an Assistant Corporation Counsel for the city of Syracuse for nearly a decade, providing him with and in-depth knowledge of municipal operations. After leaving city hall in 2018, he shifted to family court appeals and currently works for Hiscock Legal Aid, which provides free legal counsel to low-income residents of Onondaga County.

With the mayoral election set for November 4, the Onondaga County Libertarian Party urges voters support Tom Babilon’s campaign for a more efficient, accountable, and liberty-minded city government. For more information, visit gobabilon. com

articles.summary: A Libertarian plan to cut $6.3 trillion from the federal budget, covering military spending, agency eliminations, student loans, gold purchases and sequencing tax cuts after spending cuts.

body.text: Although President Trump and his friend Elon Musk have made a good start in regard to reducing the size of the federal workforce, they have a long way to go as far as reducing the national budget is concerned. This is due to the fact that they require the assistance of the Republican and Democrat parties, who are a combination of clueless and irresponsible.

The 2024 deficit for the national government was $1.832.86 trillion. The deficit for the first 5 months of fiscal 2025 (October-February) was a record $1.147 trillion. The projected deficit for the year is over $3.4 trillion.
The National Debt is over $36 trillion dollars.

The only response from the Republicans and Democrats was to pass another “temporary spending bill to fund the government for another 6 months” in March. Their bill will cut national government spending by $7 billion dollars, which would be a cut of 0.103% from the previous year, unless the increase in interest on the national debt is included. When interest on the national debt is included ($952 billion in 2024, over $1 trillion in 2025), their bill is a spending increase.
This was followed by the proposed big, bad, unlimited spending bill to “fund Trump’s agenda.” It will bankrupt the country. Anyone who thinks that is the best we can do should rethink their position.

Since that is not acceptable, the following is a Libertarian alternative. The achievable goal is for a balanced national budget or yearly surplus in ONE YEAR. The maximum time for this is to occur is 6 years or less. A drastic reduction of economic interventionism occurs as the national budget is sharply reduced.

“Moreover, a drastic cut in the government budget--both in taxes and expenditures--will of itself speed adjustment by changing the social choice toward more saving and investment relative to consumption.

For government spending, whatever the label attached to it, is solely consumption. Any cut in the budget, therefore, raises the investment-consumption ratio in the economy and allows more rapid validation of originally wasteful and loss-yielding projects.” - Murray Rothbard, “America’s Great Depression”, p. 167
The Congressional Budget Office stated the budget expense was $6.2 trillion for 2023, $6.8 trillion in 2024.
Procedure for Cutting the National Budget
1. Eliminate the yearly expense for housing, education and loans at the national level.
Totals for 2023 according to the Congressional Budget Office:

Housing and Urban Development (HUD) total is $252.84 billion. Department of Education total is $174.97 billion. There are 118 programs that provide credit assistance. The total amount for 2024 is projected at $2.2 trillion. New direct loans total $171 billion. New loan guarantees total $2.0 trillion.

Eliminate $23 billion in “Climate adaptation and resilience” for Departments of Commerce, Interior, Homeland Security, Agriculture, EPA, Pentagon and Army Corps of Engineers “to address the increasing severity of extreme weather events fueled by climate change.”
Eliminate $325 billion in paid family and medical leave of 12 weeks for eligible workers.
Eliminate foreign aid, a $60.4 billion cut.
All taxpayer-funded payments to illegal (or ‘undocumented’) immigrants are eliminated, reducing expenses by the current estimate of $180 billion per year.
Eliminate $50 billion+ wasted Yearly on buying the union vote with Unnecessary road projects.
Returning to a constitutionally limited and non-interventionist foreign policy will lead to a massive reduction in the bloated $800 billion plus military budget.
Plan on a Steady and Continuing Yearly Military Budget Reduction.
The first year target is $100 billion.
Ultimately, the goal is a 50% reduction.

The foreign policy of the U.S. has been less than exemplary for quite a long time. We will start with the fact that the United States has bombed at least 32 countries without a preceding declaration of war since the end of World War II and go on from there.

Once this issue is addressed, the U.S. responsibility to restore Constitutional foreign policy could then be addressed. The end of an interventionist foreign policy will be one result. It will also create a foundation where the end of economic interventionism will follow logically.
2A. Military Budget Reduction/Compensation for Crimes Committed
Compensation will be deducted from the military budget and paid to foreign governments for 4 foreign policy crimes:
- Bombing a foreign country without a preceding declaration of war. - Attempting or succeeding in overthrowing the government of a foreign country without a preceding declaration of war.
- Placing economic sanctions on a foreign country without a preceding declaration of war.
- Any country that had toxins dropped on their country as part of an undeclared war would be entitled to compensation for this infraction.
This includes dropped pesticides, herbicides, etc. as was done as part of the “War on Drugs”.
It also includes dropping things like napalm on a country during undeclared wars. (As was done in Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia, for example.)
One billion dollars to each country per infraction would be deducted from the military budget.

Budgetary reduction will therefore occur through a modern adaptation of the Eric-fine for Homicide, which was a feature of Celtic and Viking law. It was a payment made as compensation for killing a man of the field of battle, which is homicide.
The U.S will pay the Eric-fine only once per violation, and wipe the slate clean.
So if a country was bombed 10 times by the U.S. without a preceding declaration of war, they would receive $1 billion dollars once.
$3.568.21 TRILLION has been cut to this point.

Its first budget in fiscal year 2021 was $15.3 billion, and it grew to $18 billion in 2022. It jumped to $26.3 billion in 2023 due to internal funds transfers from the Space Development Agency and the Air Force, plus a congressional add-on. March 13, 2023.
Their proposed budget is $30 billion for 2024.

Privatize NASA. Their 2023 budget was $25.4 billion, a 5.6% increase over the previous year. Their budget is $32.41 billion if the amount distributed among ‘sub-components’ is included. They also have many assets to sell.
Phase Out of Fed: Yearly 1% sale of assets= $90 billion per year
$3.568.21 trillion +$30 billion +$32.41 billion +90 Billion =$3.720.62 TRILLION CUT
Eliminate the CIA. Ron Paul put their budget at roughly $75 billion in 2012.
A description of the ‘Incompetence and outrageousness of the CIA’ is available in the book “Legacy of Ashes,” by New York Times Pulitzer prize winner Tim Winer. Also, in many other places.
Eliminating or reducing the highly politicized FBI-amount unknown.
Sale of FBI and CIA assets-buildings, land, etc. -amount unknown
Close to $4 Trillion Has Been Cut to This Point.

“As of 2023, the Fed owns $2.6 trillion of mortgage securities. That is larger than what the total assets of the Fed were at the end of 2008. In my view, the Federal Reserve should get out of the business of pushing up housing prices, and the Fed’s mortgage portfolio should go back to the normal amount of exactly zero.” - Alex J. Pollock, pp. 8-9, “The Austrian,” May-June 2023

As of June 2024, the Fed held approximately $2.3 trillion in Mortgage Backed Securities, almost 30% of the outstanding balance in the Agency MBS market. The Fed should sell them all and leave the MBS market.

A requirement to pay all debts is included. Political debt forgiveness will end immediately. ’Government’ provided student loans, in particular, must all be repaid. The U.S. government has been destroying education for decades. “Forgiving Student Loan Debt” is the government’s way of pardoning itself and continuing the same process.

For many victims of the U.S. Educational system (a.k.a. ‘students’), discovering why debts must be repaid will be the first thing they have learned from the government educational system. They will have a chance to learn how badly they have been cheated, and why it is important to stop this from continuing.
(On a related note, government ‘debt forgiveness’ counts as taxable income, so they get us coming and going.)
Student loan debt repayments to resume. $1.78 trillion due as of the first quarter of 2023.
(This occurs in a country where College Football teams composed of unpaid players routinely sell out 80,000 seat stadiums.)
Combine these two items and it is obvious that the U.S. national government should be removed from all college loans.
Union pension funds alone were over $700 billion short by 2021. Trump was prosecuting union officials. Biden stopped it.
Over $1.78 trillion + Over $700 billion = $2.5 trillion plus is due.
At least $8.8 trillion over several years is eliminated.
5. Eliminating Unconstitutional or Redundant National Government Agencies

The total Amount to be eliminated is unknown, but it is substantial. The national government currently contains 440 agencies and 2 million employees. The following is an improvement on the procedure being utilized by President Trump and his friend Elon Musk.

All national government agencies will be reviewed, all that are unconstitutional and/or counterproductive will be eliminated or phased out at the national level. This means that most national government agencies will be eliminated over time.
Not only is the yearly budget expense eliminated, but also all the unnecessary costs they place on honest Americans.

This will be done with minimal disruption to the labor market in the following manner. In the year that an agency is eliminated, all the current employees will receive their full salary, whether or not they get a different job.
So in the first year the agency is eliminated except for the cost of salaries, in the second year the cost is reduced to zero.
Additionally, all assets (land, buildings, etc.) are sold to the private sector.
Eliminate the National Labor Board, and any rules they have implemented.

These geniuses have turned a ‘strike’ into a brilliant negotiating strategy. It’s not. If you have a job and refuse to show up, you quit. You may receive your job back, but you are not entitled to it. Massive savings for businesses occurs, employees benefit greatly, a massive reduction in economic interventionism occurs. Eliminate the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and any rules they have implemented. Actual safety is dependent on the individual. The real purpose of the NHTSA, like many government agencies, is to mandate optional, expensive and unnecessary items. (The mandatory “Safety Measure” Air bags are an example.)

“From 1996 to 2000, 191 people, including 116 children, died in cases in which an air bag was or was suspected to be the cause. In many cases, the deaths came in low-speed crashes, in which the force of the deploying air bags proved fatal.” NewYork Times, Aug. 30, 2001
The NHTSA solution? Mandatory placement of children in the back seat.

Automakers always comply, since they not only pass on the cost, the price becomes INFINITY once it is mandated. An incredible markup is permitted. A market with a price level of infinity is not a competitive market. NHTSA does this all the time.

Eliminate the NHTSA and massive savings for consumers will occur, safety enhanced, and a tremendous competitive market will ensue. Redundant: Homeland Security-Abolish, and return responsibilities to pre 9/11 agencies.
Close to $10 trillion over several years will be eliminated.
6. A Small Move toward a Gold Standard and Sound Currency

Each year the national government will take 1% of tax revenue and purchase gold. The gold must be held for at least 3 years, so this will not be a mere bookkeeping transaction. State and local governments should also do this.
Additionally, 1/10 of 1 percent will be used to buy silver. The country will therefore be making a small move toward a gold and silver Standard.
7. Spending Cuts Must Precede Tax Cuts
This is the alternative to the Republicans’ recently passed “Big, Bad, Reaganesque Fraud of an Unlimited Deficit Spending” bill, which will bankrupt the country.
There is much more involved in a Libertarian plan to cut the budget, but cutting $6.3 trillion is enough of an outline for now.
Spending cuts must precede tax cuts, creating a verifiable arithmetical progression downward.
Each tax bracket will be expanded yearly by $1,000 per year and each tax rate will be reduced by one percentage point per year. There should be no tax on savings, inheritance, or capital gains.
This can only be done if spending cuts precede tax cuts.

articles.title: Ed Clark 1930–2025
articles.summary: LPNY mourns its founding chair Ed Clark, the 1980 Libertarian presidential nominee, who died on June 19, 2025, at age 95.

body.text: The Libertarian Party of New York mourns the passing of Edward Emerson “Ed” Clark, the LPNY founding chair and a trailblazer for the modern liberty movement. Clark, who passed away on June 19, 2025, at the age of 95, leaves behind a legacy as one of the most influential early figures in the party’s history.

Clark’s journey with the Libertarian movement began in 1971, when he left the Republican Party in response to President Richard Nixon’s wage and price controls, a moment that galvanized many who would go on to shape the Libertarian Party. When the New York Free Libertarian Party was organized in 1972, Clark was the first State Chair, helping lay the groundwork for what would become one of the party’s most enduring affiliates.

After his time in New York, Clark moved west, where he continued to shape the Libertarian Party on a national scale. He was elected Vice-Chair of the Libertarian National Committee in 1972 and later served as State Chair of the Libertarian Party of California. In 1978, he made headlines running for Governor of California, earning 377,960 votes—5.46% of the vote—a record for a Libertarian gubernatorial candidate that still stands. Two years later, Clark carried the party’s banner as its 1980 presidential nominee alongside running mate David Koch, earning over 920,000 votes nationwide and cementing the Libertarian Party’s status as a credible national force.

Beyond his campaigns, Clark will be remembered for his calm, professional demeanor and his ability to communicate libertarian principles to new audiences, often describing libertarianism as “low-tax liberalism” to reach voters across the spectrum. His 1980 campaign sparked the creation of Students for Clark groups nationwide, inspired countless activists, and brought libertarian ideas—tax reduction, deregulation, civil liberties, and nonintervention abroad—into the national conversation.

Ed Clark’s pioneering efforts as the founding Chair of the Libertarian Party of New York and his groundbreaking national campaigns helped shape the trajectory of the party. We honor his contributions and his role in giving our party, in New York and across the country, a strong foundation to build upon.

articles.title: Matthew Morgan Wins Spot on Ballot
articles.author: Christopher Skelly
articles.summary: A court restored Brooklyn Libertarian Matthew Morgan to the ballot for New York City Council District 39 after an elections board removal.

body.text: Brooklyn, NY -- The Kings County Supreme Court ordered that Matthew Morgan of the Brooklyn Libertarian Party, and the Libertarian candidate for New York City Council District 39, be placed back on the ballot this week. Morgan was removed from the ballot by the Board of Elections in the City of New York in June due to a cover sheet error. Honorary Judge Lawrence Knipel found that the Board of Elections had erred in its decision to remove Morgan from the ballot for his defective cover sheet, and that he had shown substantial compliance with state election laws and had made no errors worthy of disqualification. Matthew Morgan will therefore be on the ballot for the November 4, 2025 General Election. He was previously on the ballot for the 2021 General Election, running for the same position against the same candidates. Morgan is campaigning on the same issues now as he was then: building more housing, abolishing zoning, saving small businesses, reforming the police department, removing ICE, and promoting a more environmentally friendly, pedestrian-oriented, and alternative transportation–focused city.

When he is not campaigning, Morgan has spent the past half-decade in various leadership roles in service organizations such as Rotary International, as well as in local mutual aid and immigrant outreach groups.

“I believe that my experience and expertise working in the private sector and within numerous service organizations have uniquely qualified me to be the strongest candidate in this race. I know the neighborhood, I know the neighbors, I know the struggles, and I know how we can improve the district and improve the city. I look forward to sharing those ideas and solutions in the coming months leading up to the election.”

articles.summary: LPNY mourns longtime Libertarian activist, mathematics professor and former candidate Donald Silberger, who died July 22, 2025, at age 95.

body.text: The Libertarian Party of New York mourns the loss of longtime party activist and candidate, Donald “Don” Silberger, who died on July 22, 2025, at the age of 95.

He was deeply involved in the Libertarian Party of New York, serving as a candidate for statewide office multiple times, a Presidential Elector in several national elections, and holding leadership roles locally and on the State Committee, including a term as a Vice-Chair of the party.
Silberger was born on February 26, 1930, in York, Pennsylvania and graduated from York High School.

He earned a scholarship to Harvard University and attended medical school, later teaching high school physics and chemistry for two years in East Cleveland. He then pursued graduate studies at the University of Washington, and earned his PhD in mathematics.

He became a mathematics professor at SUNY New Paltz, where he also served as faculty advisor for a college libertarian group in the late 1990s. He discovered libertarianism around 1991 and quickly became an active member of the Libertarian Party.

He ran for public office several times as a Libertarian. In 1998, he was the party’s nominee for Lieutenant Governor of New York alongside gubernatorial candidate Chris Garvey. He ran again for Lieutenant Governor in 2006 with gubernatorial candidate John Clifton. In 2004, he was the party’s candidate for U.S. Senate. He also served as a Libertarian Presidential Elector for Harry Browne (1996, 2000), Michael Badnarik (2004), and Bob Barr (2008).

Within the Libertarian Party of New York, Silberger served in many leadership roles. He was Chair and State Representative for the Hudson Valley Libertarian Party during the 1990s and early 2000s. He was elected three times as a Member-at-Large of the State Committee (2001-2002; 2006-2008) and later served as Vice-Chair of the LPNY from 2010 to 2011.
In his 2004 U.S. Senate campiang website autobiography, he described himself as a “former self-declared liberal” who realized that libertarianism better represented his long-held values.

articles.title: U.S. Debt
articles.author: Rick Miller
articles.summary: Rick Miller responds to popular online claims about the national debt, arguing that spending on defense and entitlements, not taxes on the rich or immigrants, is the core problem.

body.text: ‘If only the rich paid their taxes…’
‘If we put illegal immigrants in 4-star hotels instead of 5-star hotels the country wouldn’t have these problems’
I looked online to see what opinions there were about the U.S. defaulting on its debt. There were well-thought-out views and there were views such as above.
The quoted views are emotional conclusions. If only people would do a fact check before making statements such as these.

With respect to the rich; the rich do pay more taxes than any other group, and by more, I mean not only number of dollars but percentages as well. That’s not to deny there are some deductions (loopholes if you prefer) that should be eliminated.
What about those illegals destroying government budgets because we spend so much money on them?

It is easy to blame this group. What we spend on illegal immigrants is small compared to government spending on defense, Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid. We must address these programs if we hope to get control of our government’s dangerous fiscal condition, by which I mean its debt.
I cite these examples to illustrate how the left and right use scapegoats. The fact is that under Democratic rule we get $2 trillion dollar deficits and under Republican rule we get the same.

One of the well-thought-out online views about U.S. debt is from the University of Pennsylvania business school. It concluded we have maybe 20 years to get our fiscal house in order to avoid the financial catastrophe of debt default. Another is a Brookings Institute survey of the debt and how serious our problem is.
The government can avoid default for a time by creating more money.
That is, of course, a catastrophe; it is simply a postponed default that creates conditions such as Zimbabwe and The Weimar Republic experienced.

articles.title: Education Choice and Property Rights
articles.author: Vincent O’Neill
articles.summary: Proposes withdrawal of consent from school taxes, phased-out charter school funding and a property-tax overhaul to give families educational choice.

body.text: Property Rights will be improved through creating educational choice based on the withdrawal of consent.
The purpose of Public Schools is control, not education.

The issue of educational choice, and the related question of educational quality, is supremely important. Two proposed solutions fail to address the real problem, while also creating additional problems.
One proposal to address the issue is through the use of ‘tuition tax credits’; another is through “charter schools.”
A variable tax credit will leave taxpayers continually at the mercy of Republicans and Democrats. Varying levels of ‘tax credits’ will continually be manipulated to the detriment of everyone.

The problem with “charter schools” is that although they are currently marginally better than public schools, they are continually lowering their quality and amount to little more than a Trojan horse to end private schools altogether.
The problem was summed up by Ludwig Von Mises:

“The school thus becomes the source of irreconcilable national conflict and ‘a political prize of highest importance.’ With respect to the debate over compulsory education, Mises emphasizes, the only effective solution is to de-politicize schooling by abolishing both compulsory education laws and political involvement with schools, leaving the education of children “entirely to parents and to private associations and institutions”. Joseph Salerno, “Nation, Migration, and Trade,” pp. 14-15.
The proper solution therefore becomes obvious.
The basis for addressing the issues of school and property tax and educational choice is the withdrawal of consent.
Withdrawal of Consent, the School Tax and Educational Choice
1. If you never attended public schools, you never consented to them, and should be exempt from school tax.
2. If you attended public schools but have children in private schools instead, you will be exempt from the school tax for any first through 12th grade year that you have children in private schools.
The school tax resumes for these people after their children graduate, since they previously consented to the public school system through their previous attendance.
3. Businesses should NOT pay the school tax. Only individuals who have been or currently are part of the system should pay.

Businesses are not people and have therefore never consented. The school tax portion of the property tax should either be entirely eliminated immediately, or steadily reduced as part of a longer term complete phase out.
It is important to make a good start in this direction.

An example would be steady 5% or 10% reductions each year, for a minimum of 6 consecutive years. This will provide a large and steady tax reduction, improve business profitability, provide increased employment opportunities, and increase competition between localities.
Charter schools must move away from public funding and towards fully private funding.
An arithmetical progression will provide the foundation.
Charter schools taxpayer funding will be reduced by 1% per year for first 3 years, 2% per year for next 3 years, 3% for next 3 years, 4% for next 3 years, etc.
The charter schools will gradually raise the tuition charged, and also ask for private donations.
Current taxpayer funding is the limit.
Funding will be eliminated for the following expenses: Transportation, School Psychologist and Pensions.
Transportation in particular is a large and lucrative market requiring competition.
The purpose of a school psychologist is to protect teaching failures.
On the other hand, if a parent wants to send his child to a psychologist, they are free to do so and accept the cost. School employees are not qualified to make this judgement.
Pensions, when not required by law, should not be provided.
B. Ask graduates of the school, and others who live in the school district, for voluntary contributions to make up the revenue loss.
C. Reduce the number of employees
The U.S. Department of Education reports that since 1950, the number of K-12 public school students has increased 96%.
The number of public school teachers increased 243%.
The total number of public school employees has increased by 709%, according to the Heritage Foundation.
The Current System of Property Assessments

Yearly property tax assessments are based on ‘estimated market value of a property.’ Market values can fluctuate due to various factors, including the local real estate market, economic conditions, and recent sales of comparable homes.
In addition, improvements and alterations increase assessed value. You are penalized financially for improving your home.
All of these factors provide Republicans and Democrats excuses to raise your property tax without a vote.
The major change is this. The assessed value should be the price you paid for the home. Period.
It will not constantly increase so Republicans and Democrats can perpetually raise our taxes without a vote.
This one item gives everyone a property tax cut.
State and local taxes should be cut at the state and local level.

articles.title: In Memoriam: James “Jim” Rosenbeck 1954–2025
articles.summary: LPNY mourns Jim Rosenbeck, a retired school counselor from Genesee County who served as State Chair from 2018 to 2020 and ran as a Libertarian candidate.

body.text: The Libertarian Party of New York mourns the loss of James “Jim” Rosenbeck, who passed away on September 8, 2025 at the age of 71. Jim was a dedicated activist, leader, and longtime advocate for liberty whose contributions were especially influential in the late 2010s.

A retired school counselor and Genesee County resident, Jim earned his Master of Science in Educational Counseling from SUNY Brockport in 1981 and served as Counseling Department Chairperson at Pembroke High School before retiring. He then devoted much of his time to political and community activism.

Jim’s involvement in the Libertarian Party began in the early 2010s with the Genesee County Libertarian Party. He served as Secretary, chaired the City of Batavia Libertarian Committee, and represented the county affiliate on the State Committee. From 2015 to 2018 he served as Vice-Chair of the LPNY, working closely with State Chair Mark Glogowski.

In 2018, Jim was elected State Chair, serving until April 2020. He led the party during a pivotal period when Larry Sharpe ran for Governor for the first time, and subsequently achieved ballot access for the party for the first time. He also briefly represented Region 8 on the Libertarian National Committee in 2018. He was a Delegate to the 2014, 2016, and 2018 Libertarian National Conventions and served as New York’s Delegation Chair in 2018.
In addition to leadership in the party, Jim ran as a Libertarian candidate for Batavia City Council twice, in 2013 and 2017. He was also a Presidential Elector for Gary Johnson/Bill Weld in 2016.

Jim was active in the party alongside his wife, Deborah Kerr-Rosenbeck, and encouraged others to take part in the political process. Jim was committed to building the Libertarian Party, through working to develop new county affiliates, support candidates for public office, and petition to secure ballot access, and other activities.
His advocacy left a lasting mark and will be remembered by his family, friends, and many fellow Libertarians.

articles.title: New York’s Shift from Natural Gas: A Case for a Jones Act LNG Waiver
articles.author: Rich Purtell
articles.summary: Argues that New York’s move away from natural gas raises energy costs and that a Jones Act waiver for liquefied natural gas shipping deserves consideration.

body.text: New York State’s ongoing transition away from natural gas is emblematic of a broader push toward renewable energy and reduced carbon emissions. While this shift aligns with ambitious climate goals, it also highlights a critical issue for neighboring New England states: the need for reliable, affordable energy during the transition. This challenge underscores the importance of revisiting the Jones Act—a century-old maritime law—to allow domestic liquefied natural gas (LNG) to flow to New England.

The Jones Act, formally known as Section 27 of the Merchant Marine Act of 1920, requires goods transported between U.S. ports to be carried on ships that are U.S.-flagged, U.S.-built, U.S.-owned, and U.S.-crewed. This creates barriers for energy distribution, including LNG.

The United States is the world’s leading exporter of LNG, with tankers regularly transporting the fuel to dozens of countries. Last year, for example, the Cove Point, Maryland LNG terminal exported LNG as far as Japan and India. Yet incredibly— and absurdly—that same LNG can’t be sent up the coast to New England due to a complete lack of U.S.-built and U.S.-flagged LNG tankers.

Instead, the region often relies on costlier foreign LNG imports. Earlier this year, the CEO of ISO New England highlighted the benefits that relief from the Jones Act would provide. Testifying before Congress, he pointed out that LNG was being imported at approximately six times the price that US LNG exports command.

New York’s pivot away from natural gas compounds this issue. As the state phases out natural gas infrastructure and prioritizes electrification and renewable energy, it reduces its role as a transit hub for natural gas pipelines to New England. This leaves New England states, which already face some of the highest energy costs in the nation, even more vulnerable to supply shortages during peak demand periods, such as harsh winters.
A Jones Act waiver for LNG could provide a practical solution. By allowing non-compliant vessels to transport LNG between U.S. ports, New England could access abundant and affordable domestic LNG.

This would reduce reliance on foreign imports, enhance energy security, and stabilize prices for consumers. Moreover, domestic LNG is often produced under stricter environmental and labor standards than foreign alternatives, aligning with broader sustainability and ethical goals.

A Jones Act LNG waiver would not only support New England’s energy needs but also strengthen the nation’s energy independence. As policymakers weigh the complexities of energy and environmental policy, pragmatic solutions like this deserve serious consideration.

articles.title: Adopting a Just Immigration Policy
articles.author: Vincent O’Neill
articles.summary: Proposes “A Just Immigration Policy”: sponsorship by individual citizens, a five-year wait without taxpayer aid, no amnesty and an end to taxpayer-funded services for illegal immigrants.

body.text: “You can’t have open immigration and a welfare state.” - Milton Friedman
“It was not easy to become a citizen of Athens.” - Herodotus, “The Histories”
The immigration policy of the United States left a lot to be desired for quite a long time, but the antics of the Biden administration brought it to a series of new lows.

The ridiculous actions of the Biden administration at the southern border when it first assumed the presidency should have been countered immediately. Instead, an absurd downward spiral has been allowed to continue undisturbed, bringing us to the situation we face now.

Despite that fact, the situation we face is easily overcome. All that is necessary is for the U.S. government to finally adopt “A Just Immigration Policy”. Once such a policy is proposed, the powers that be must either refute it or implement it. They won’t be able to ignore it.
A Very Brief Description of “A Just Immigration Policy”
In general, A Just Immigration Policy consists of immigration that is invited, sponsored, and self-sufficient at least until citizenship is achieved.
The requirements to achieve citizenship will be the same for all immigrants.
There is a little more to it, however.

The only discussion of the immigration issue in this country occurs on a completely dishonest level. Immigration should be invited, sponsored, and reserved for those who do not require the assistance of U.S. taxpayers during their waiting period to become a U.S. citizen.

The most important issue to be addressed is whether or not illegal (or ‘undocumented’) immigrants, as well as those going through the legal citizenship process, should be entitled to any taxpayer-funded service.
The response of far too many Democrat and Republican politicians is a resounding YES.

Amazingly enough, this is the one part of any immigration debate that Republicans and Democrats always avoid. Not surprisingly, resolving this one issue would lead to implementation of a reasonable policy. If someone is self-sufficient until they become a citizen, chances are they will continue to be self-sufficient.
The United States currently spends $180 billion per year on services for illegal immigrants.
Illegal (or ‘undocumented’) immigrants are entitled to receive nothing at taxpayer expense.
Americans should be more aware of the manner in which the immigration issue is being used.

Instead of a debate about human rights, responsibility and freedom, the issue of illegal (or ‘undocumented’) immigration is being used to expand the (misnamed) ‘welfare state’, judicial overreach and tyranny, the police state, the ‘war on drugs’, economic interventionism, harassment of employers, expanded government spending at all levels, expanded budget and responsibilities for the ‘Department of Homeland Security’, expanding the vote to additional ‘welfare state’ recipients, and every other ‘bait and switch’ you can think of.

If illegal immigrants were in this country but outside the law and the welfare state, they would have to rely on voluntary human action. They would have to recreate the voluntary associations and human interdependence which (largely) prevailed in this country before the institution of the income tax.
Recreating these voluntary associations will happen to all those who become citizens through a just immigration policy that treats all potential citizens the same.
Getting them to rely on the ‘welfare’ state destroys this.

“On another level, the effort to cleanse the system of politically incorrect tendencies is taking on a mass character with a campaign to replace the electorate.” “How is this being done? Simple. Legalize voting by illegal aliens.” - Justin Raimondo, Chronicles, November, 2017, p.42
That insight is from 2017. The situation is much worse today. The main concern of most Democrats and Republicans is to provide a path to the welfare state and the ballot box.

Immigrants, legal or not, are therefore considered more likely to vote for the welfare state and its politicians. This is the same way the vote-buying ‘welfare’ state was created and spread in the first place, and that most current voters have seen through.
Rather than relying on the Ballot Box, the question should be removed from the political process and its endless posturing, and transferred directly to the citizen.
Your vote will be expressed by either becoming a sponsor, or declining to do so. Ultimate democracy therefore becomes the purest expression of one man/one vote.
Voting on the issue of expanded immigration, or to provide a ‘path to citizenship’ for currently illegal immigrants, becomes a simple and inexpensive process.
Every adult citizen will control 100% of their vote on the issue of immigration, 100% of their time as a U.S. citizen.
The path to citizenship will be the same for all prospective immigrants.
The process will not be expensive.

Immigrants will have to pay a filing fee, go 5 years without U.S. taxpayer assistance, and go 5 years without being convicted of a felony or spreading infectious disease. If they accomplish this goal, they become a U.S. citizen.
They are not permitted to vote in an election until they become a citizen.
Any U.S. citizen would only be permitted to sponsor one prospective citizen at a time.
If this person then successfully becomes a citizen after 5 years, the sponsor will be permitted to do the same for another potential citizen.
4. Voting on the issue of a ‘Path to Citizenship’ for Illegal Immigrants

There were an estimated 10-12 million illegal immigrants in the U.S. as of 2020. There are many more now, but the number is unknown. Therefore, the following shows how easily this situation could have been taken care of in 2020. The same formula applies, but with a much higher number of applicants.
There are roughly 320 million citizens in the U.S. If half of them are above the age of 18, that means there are 160 million adult citizens with a vote on the issue in the coming year.
10 million of 160 million =1/16, or 6.25%. 12 million of 160 million =3/40, or 7.5%
Providing a ‘path to citizenship’ legalizing 10-12 million illegal immigrants would therefore have required the approval of less than 10% of adult U.S. citizens. That would have been no problem.
The same formula should be applied to the much larger number of illegal immigrants who are now in the country.
U.S. citizens will vote by putting their money where their mouth is, and taking responsibility for their actions.
Politicians who favor expanded immigration should lead by their own example, and sponsor a (legal or currently illegal) immigrant for U.S. citizenship.
For the illegal immigrants currently in the country, there will be two choices.
A cutoff date is necessary, and will be one year from the adoption of this proposal.
Option #1. In time for the Cutoff Date
The time limit is one year from now. ‘Now’ will start the day “A Just Immigration Policy” is enacted.
Currently illegal immigrants will have to find ONE U.S. citizen willing to sponsor them and satisfy the terms described above.

They must then go 5 years without U.S. taxpayer assistance, pay a filing fee, and go 5 years without being convicted of a felony or spreading infectious disease. If they accomplish this goal, they become a U.S. citizen.
They are not permitted to vote in an election until they become a citizen.
A sponsor provides an endorsement of the prospective citizen’s character. If someone can’t find even one U.S. citizen to sponsor them, this tells you all you need to know about them.

Until or unless they find a sponsor, they have chosen to be outside the protection of the law, and no laws (beyond obvious situations - they cannot be murdered, a victim of theft, etc.), such as minimum wage laws, apply to them.
After the cutoff date, the process is almost the same. The only difference is that they will have to return to their country of origin in order to apply for citizenship.
There will be NO AMNESTY now or ever again.
And unless someone is being sponsored for U.S. citizenship and receiving NO U.S. taxpayer assistance, they are not entitled to ‘work permits ‘either.
All current Visa programs, particularly the H-1B Visa, will end immediately. There is no shortage of American citizens available to do these jobs.
(On a related topic, there is no such thing as “a job Americans won’t do.” There are, however, jobs Americans aren’t allowed to do because of ‘minimum wage’ laws.)

Private contractual terms between employer and employee will replace the current government terms. The terms must include sponsorship for U.S. citizenship by an individual U.S. citizen, and acceptance of Potential Liability by the sponsor.
If a U.S. citizen sponsors someone for citizenship, they must also accept liability if this person fails to complete the terms required to attain citizenship.

If this occurred, the sponsor in question would no longer be an acceptable sponsor, and they would never again be permitted to sponsor a person for U.S. citizenship. The possibility of anyone sponsoring a terrorist or disreputable person would be quickly reduced to almost zero. All that will be required is for currently illegal immigrants to be given one year to find sponsor, go five years without taxpayer assistance, not commit a felony and not spread infectious disease.
Mass deportations will therefore end since they become unnecessary when taxpayer-funded services end.

This proposal creates a system which allows the maximum area for Human Action based on justice and responsibility to flourish. It is the alternative to the continual abdication of responsibility by the Republican and Democrat political class.

articles.summary: Larry Sharpe, on his third run, won the Libertarian nomination for Governor at the Rochester convention, which also elected delegates and national committee representatives.

body.text: Larry Sharpe was nominated for Governor by the Libertarian Party of New York at its 2025 Nominating Convention, held on October 25 at the Homewood Suites by Hilton in Rochester, New York.

LPNY Chair Duane Whitmer called the meeting to order. The nominations for statewide candidates were among the earlier items of business. Two candidates were nominated for Governor: Larry Sharpe and Christopher Olenski. None of the Above (NOTA) is always a choice on party ballots.
In the first and only round of voting, Sharpe was nominated after recieving 12 out of 20 votes of the State Committee. Olenski received 5 votes and 3 votes were cast for NOTA.

Other statewide offices, including Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, and Comptroller, will be filled before a March 15, 2026 deadline set by the State Committee, as the party works to assemble a full and competitive slate of candidates for 2026.

This is Sharpe’s third run for Governor. His first run in 2018 garnered over 95,000 votes and gave the Libertairan Party ballot access for the first time in New York history. However, the state budget snuck in changes to ballot access laws, increasing the signature threshold and vote requirement to get ballot access.

Sharpe’s second run occurred under these new laws in 2022, in which he had just over 42,000 raw signatures (which was more than Lee Zeldin’s raw signature account for the Independence Party line, after removing the 11,000 fraudulent signatures), but was not enough for the required 45,000 signatures. The Libertarian Party of New York and Green Party of New York were involved in a three-year court battle to overturn these requirements from 2020 to 2023.

Other business at the convention included the election of New York’s representatives to the Libertairan National Convention committees. For Platform, Onondaga County Secretary and State Platform Committee member Rose Leatherman will serve as the Represen

tative while Suffolk County Vice Chair Christian Padgett will serve as Alternate. For the Credentials Committee, State Treasurer Chance Haywood will serve as Represnetiave while Monroe County Chair Steve Becker will serve as Alternate. Additionally, 30 delegates were appointed to represent New York. Additional delegates will be appointed once an exact number is known.

The convention was concluded with remarks from LNC Region 6 Representative Patrick Ford, as well as Libertarian attorney Jamesostrowski, who is running for LNC Chair. The convention concluded with a moment of silence in honor of former statewide candidate and state Vice Chair Donald Silberger, former Chair James Rosenbeck, and LPNY founding chair and 1980 Presidential nominee Edward Clark, all who passed away in the past few months.

articles.title: Ballot Access or Boycott
articles.author: Vincent O’Neill
articles.summary: Argues that Republicans and Democrats raised New York’s ballot access thresholds after a strong Libertarian vote, and proposes reforms including a shared petition window and more signatures per voter.

body.text: The Democrats did not hold presidential primary debates in 2024, despite the fact, or because, Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. was challenging Biden for the nomination. (He then became an independent candidate for President.)

The refusal to debate challengers to the status quo is the typical response of the Democrats and Republicans. The most likely reason for this behavior is the fact that neither party has anything worthwhile to offer on any important issue.

Another particularly grievous example comes from New York. For the previous 50 years, a political party was required to have its gubernatorial candidate receive 50,000 votes in order to have guaranteed ballot status for the next 4 years.
This is what happened in the 2018 New York gubernatorial election, and its aftermath. It refers to Libertarian candidate Larry Sharpe.

“On Election Day, Sharpe received 95,033 votes (1.6%) and came in fourth place behind Cuomo, Republican challenger Marc Molinaro, and Green Party candidate Howie Hawkins. Sharpe’s vote total achieved automatic ballot access for the Libertarian Party of New York for the first time in the party’s history.
The 95,333 votes for Governor 2018 Libertarian Party Candidate Larry Sharpe received was MORE THAN 6 TIMES MORE THAN THE PARTY’S VOTE TOTAL OF 15,209 IN 2014.
The Republican Party’s percentage of the vote declined from 40.6% (to Democrat Andrew Cuomo’s 54%) in 2014 to 36.2% (to Democrat Cuomo’s 59.6%) in 2018, a decline of more than 4 percentage points.
In 2019, assorted Libertarian legislative candidates in New York received a total of 37,751 votes. This was a vast improvement over any previous year.

The response of the New York Democrats and Republicans was to retroactively change the requirement to achieve ballot access from the 50,000 votes for governor requirement of the previous 50 years to 130,000 votes every two years, on April 4, 2020 thereby, cheating the Libertarian Party of New York of its ballot access.
In addition, they also tripled the number of petition signatures required to place a candidate on the ballot, from 15,000 to 45,000.
To repeat, this was after the Libertarian Party vote total was MORE THAN 6 TIMES MORE THAN ITS TOTAL 4 YEARS BEFORE WHILE THE REPUBLICAN PARTY TOTAL DECLINED BY MORE THAN 4 PERCENTAGE POINTS.
This atrocity is a typical example of Republican and Democrat behavior.

The “Supreme Court” refused to hear the case brought to address this matter, and the only legislative solutions proposed have attracted little to no support and also fall short of addressing this atrocity. The only acceptable solution is to admit that the Libertarian Party satisfied all requirements for permanent ballot status and to restore automatic ballot status for the next four years, plus any additional time the party has been cheated of automatic ballot access.
Starting with April 4, 2020, that number is 3 election cycles and counting, bringing the current total to 5+ years and counting.

If New York Republicans and Democrats continue with this behavior, the response should be to call for a BOYCOTT of all Republican and Democrat candidates in New York State unless or until this situation is rectified. (This would be particularly easy to do to the Republicans. We’d rather have them vote Libertarian, but in addition, practically all Republicans are also on the Conservative line.)

Anything else is simply a stalling tactic designed to perpetually deny the automatic ballot status the Libertarian Party of New York earned while paying lip service to the issue and shedding a few crocodile tears.

Keep in mind that the major political reform to come out of Watergate was to create campaign finance restrictions in order to make sure that a Eugene McCarthy would never again be allowed to challenge the establishment candidate.

The Commission on Presidential Debates is an extension of this idea. Every presidential election since 1988, when they excluded Ron Paul, has been an ELECTION ABOUT NOTHING, which follows a long period of noise about nothing while avoiding real issues, which is one reason the national debt is $38 trillion and rising.
It took 9 months for the national debt to increase from $36 trillion to $37 trillion. It took a mere 73 days to go from $37 trillion to $38 trillion.
This is why an alternative to the current system designed to protect the Republican/Democrat must be proposed. Offering intelligent alternatives will be a victory as long as they are introduced.

Taxpayer-funded primaries, publicly funded elections, ranked choice voting, and the Commission on Presidential Debates which has managed to exclude everyone except the Republican and Democrat Presidential candidates are all part of the same proposal. In addition, the rules involved to receive “matching funds” are beyond absurd in New York.
All must be refuted, and alternatives proposed.
The Republicans and Democrats will have to respond.
If they fail to support them, but cannot refute them, there will be repercussions.

For all offices, from village dog catcher to President of the United States, the requirements will be the same. Ballot access will require 1,000 signatures from registered voters. The time frame to get them will be the two months from late spring to early summer, May 1 to July 1.
Registered voters will be permitted to sign for more than one candidate.
Individual parties can enact their own requirements for candidates in addition to this.

articles.author: Andrew Kolstee
articles.summary: New York’s 2026 Libertarian National Convention delegation has 33 delegates, down from 2024; the article lists the 30 delegates appointed so far.

body.text: Recently, the LNC Secretary Evan McMahon posted the final delegate numbers for all the states for the 2026 National Convention. The cut off was October 31, 2025. New York, as a result, has 33 delegates.

This is a decrease of 8 delegates from the 2024 convention, where there were 41 delegates. This is attributed to the drop in votes for the Libertarian Party Presidential cnadidate. In 2020, Jo Jorgensen had over 60,000 votes in New York, while on the ballot. In 2024, Chase Oliver, who was a write-in candidate, only garnered over 5,000 votes. The lack of votes for Oliver directly resulted in the decrease of New York’s delegation number.

Even though it was not enough, the Libertarian Party of New York is grateful for those who supported Chase Oliver as a write-in candidate, as voters for our candidate help our delegate count and are crucial for ballot access.

At the nominating convention of October 25, 2025, the number of delegates remained uncertain, and so only 30 were voted upon based on the rubric. An additional 3 delegates will be confirmed, along with the Alternates, in January 2026. Note than you can still reach out if you would like to be an Alternate Delegate. New York ended up with 15 Alternates in 2024, and the 15th Alternate ended up getting promoted to Delegate during the convention.

articles.title: LPNY Denounces Oswego Common Council’s Property Rights Violation
articles.summary: LPNY condemns the Oswego Common Council’s December 2025 action against a resident’s portable wheelchair ramp as a violation of property rights.

body.text: DECEMBER 15, 2025 - The Libertarian Party of New York condemns the Oswego Common Council’s 7-0 vote to revoke Anthony Schmitt’s permission to maintain a wheelchair ramp on his property, ordering its removal over his refusal to sign a waiver and pay a fee for minor encroachment on public space.

This exemplifies government overreach violating property rights and liberty. Schmitt built a portable ramp that flips up to avoid obstructing the sidewalk, accommodating a family member’s disability. The city’s demands amount to regulatory extortion, ignoring common sense and compassion.
Property owners should control their land without interference, absent harm to others. This ramp poses no real threat.
We urge Oswego officials to reverse this decision, respect individual rights, and halt coercive local regulations. New Yorkers need freedom from unnecessary government burdens.

articles.title: LPNY Condemns Passage of COPA
articles.summary: LPNY opposes the New York City Council’s passage of COPA, arguing it infringes private property rights and will drive up housing costs, and urges a mayoral veto.

body.text: DECEMBER 29, 2025 - The Libertarian Party of New York strongly opposes the recent passage of the Community Opportunity to Purchase Act (COPA) by the New York City Council on December 18, 2025.

This legislation represents a blatant infringement on private property rights, a core principle we hold sacred. By mandating that owners of certain multifamily residential buildings grant qualified nonprofits a right of first offer and right of first refusal before selling to private buyers, COPA effectively imposes government-forced preferences in voluntary transactions. Property owners should have the unfettered right to sell their assets to whomever they choose, at terms they negotiate freely, without interference from the state or favored third parties.

While proponents claim COPA will preserve affordable housing and combat displacement, it achieves the opposite in practice. Such interventions distort the housing market, discourage investment, prolong sales processes, and ultimately reduce the supply of available properties, driving up costs for all New Yorkers.
True solutions to housing affordability lie in reducing government barriers: eliminating excessive regulations, zoning restrictions, and taxes that stifle new construction and renovation.

We call on Mayor Adams to veto this bill and urge the City Council to reject any overrides. New Yorkers deserve freedom, not more coercive mandates that erode individual liberty under the guise of social good.
