articles.title: Judicial Reform
articles.author: Vincent O’Neill
articles.summary: Proposes reforms to the court system: majority-based jury verdicts after repeated votes, an end to jury stacking, limits on bail and a “loser pays” rule for failed suits.

body.text: “Excessive bail shall not be required, nor excessive fines imposed, nor cruel and unusual punishments inflicted.” - Eighth Amendment

“A common argument defense lawyers make when trying to get courts to dismiss evidence obtained illegally against their client is that it was “the fruit of the poisoned tree”. The PATRIOT Act itself was the fruit of the tree of law enforcement’s relentless desire to be free of the inconveniences of the Fourth amendment and its guiding principles of privacy and due process.” - Brian Doherty, p. 17, Reason Magazine, November, 2021
A system of justice must replace the current ‘legal system as a Cash Cow’ system we have now.
1. Guilt, Innocence, and the Right to Trial by Jury
Requiring a unanimous verdict is a strategy used to cheat the defendant and guarantee a conviction. A very simple change eliminates this injustice.

If a unanimous verdict is required, anything less is an acquittal. According to the U.S. system, this is a ‘hung jury’, and a do-over occurs. The ‘government,’ which never pays its bills but has access to unlimited taxpayer funding, can now keep a defendant,whose funds are limited, going to court forever.
This is a recipe for deliberate dishonesty and the elimination of the right to a jury trial. It also explains the incredibly high percentage of cases which result in a ‘plea bargain.”

Once jury deliberation begins, juries will have as many business days as they require to reach a verdict. They can have as many votes each day as they like. The only one that counts is the last of the day.
They can vote on a maximum of 3 days.
The first vote must be unanimous for a conviction.
The second vote must be at least 11 of 12 for a conviction.
The third vote must be at least 9 of 12 for a conviction.
If any day’s last vote is less than 9 of 12 for conviction, it is an acquittal.

Anything less is not a “Hung Jury” or a “mistrial.” It is an acquittal. Jurors should not be forced to change their decision in order to reach an artificial unanimity. This will allow them to maintain their integrity.
End stacking the jury, which is actually taught in U.S. “Law Schools”
Judge will ask prospective jurors if they know either lawyer, or the plaintiff, or the defendant. Anyone who does will be dismissed.

The Judge will also ask prospective jurors if they are prejudiced for or against the plaintiff or defendant to such an extent that they will be unable to provide a just verdict based on the evidence. Anyone who answers in the affirmative will be dismissed.
Additionally, each lawyer receives 2 peremptory challenges only.

Although the Constitution forbids the institution of excessive bail, another strategy used by the prosecution is to keep a defendant who can’t make bail in jail indefinitely ‘awaiting trial.’ “Excessive Bail” is any amount a defendant cannot reasonably afford. Therefore, limits should be in place.

If a defendant is unable to make bail after two weeks, the bail is excessive and should be cut in half. If the defendant is still unable to make bail after an additional two weeks, it should be cut in half again. This will make sure that excessive bail cannot be imposed and will guarantee the defendant’s right to a jury trial.
The other extreme, the abolition of bail, is also unacceptable. These simple changes will create the basis for a just system to replace the “Judicial System as Cash Cow” that we have now.
One final addition will be necessary.
4. “Loser Pays” If he brought the suit

In the English Legal System, the loser is responsible for the winning party’s legal costs, including attorney’s fees. This is an excellent way to get rid of frivolous and/or meritless lawsuits, but it needs one small improvement.

The improvement is to institute “Loser Pays,” but only if he brought the suit. This is an improvement on the English system of “Loser Pays,” since it eliminates the advantage a wealthy party would otherwise hold.

articles.title: 2026 State of the State Response
articles.subtitle: Hochul’s “Affordability” Agenda: More Taxes, More Control, Less Freedom
articles.author: Libertarian Party of New York
articles.summary: LPNY answers Governor Hochul’s 2026 State of the State, arguing her “affordability” agenda means more taxes and control and calling for tax relief instead.

body.text: Governor Kathy Hochul’s 2026 State of the State address once again promises to make life “more affordable” through a massive wishlist of government programs, subsidies, and regulations, over 200 initiatives, including a push toward universal child care, more subway barriers and policing, crackdowns on 3D-printed firearms, online “protections” for kids, and various energy and housing reforms that involve even more state intervention.
I have one simple question for the Governor: When has Albany ever made life truly more affordable by doing more instead of less?

New Yorkers are crushed under the highest taxes in the nation, sky-high energy bills, crushing housing costs driven by endless zoning red tape and mandates, and a regulatory state that strangles small businesses and drives families out. Yet the response from Albany is always the same: more spending, more programs, more bureaucrats, more strings attached.
The core belief of the Libertarian Party of New York is clear: Government should get out of the way.

End the endless cycle of taxation and spending. Slash income taxes, property taxes, and sales taxes across the board. Repeal suffocating regulations that drive up housing and business costs. Let consenting adults make their own choices in child care, energy, online life, and self-defense.

Governor Hochul talks about fighting for New York families. The real fight is against the bloated, intrusive state government she leads— one that takes our money, dictates our choices, and then promises to solve the problems it created.
New Yorkers deserve better: freedom, opportunity, and their own money back in their pockets.

articles.title: The Creeping Consolidation: How New York’s Efficiency Drives Threaten Rural Liberty
articles.author: Christopher Skelly
articles.summary: Warns that state-pushed efficiency and consolidation drives, such as those in Chautauqua County, threaten local home rule and rural liberty.

body.text: Across parts of upstate New York, local autonomy is facing a direct challenge. County Leaders, citing government efficiency, are beginning to push small towns and villages to consolidate services or dissolve entirely. Now, this may appear to be fiscally responsible; however, they’re actually eroding local governance and undermining the autonomy that rural communities have the right to defend.

Chautauqua County, with a population of roughly 127,000, has expanded its Government Reduction Initiative. The 2026 budget reserves thousands of dollars for certain incentives and studies, while offering towns that agree to consolidate $50K to $100K per merger.

Defenders assert that this consolidation of services will address declining population and rising costs, and promise savings and lower property taxes. Now, sure, this sounds great! I mean, who wouldn’t be in favor of lower property taxes? What’s the issue? The issue is that these changes often depend on centralized mandates. The issue is that these programs operate under a coercive framework, funded by your dollars taken by force, essentially funding your own disempowerment. Trading away local self-rule for the illusion of efficiency is a cost no free community should accept.

For small towns like Ripley, with a population of roughly 2,300, and Mina, with a population of roughly 1,000, these kinds of incentives exploit fiscal hardship. A shrinking tax base and strict state mandates mean that ‘voluntary’ consolidation is really not a choice. When counties control funding, and smaller towns struggle to survive, a permanent loss of self-rule is traded for what is often only short-term relief. While a more genuine form of cooperation between towns would honor local control, more county-driven consolidation centralizes power. Instead, these towns might come together to share the costs of equipment, reducing costs while preserving their local identities. Creating region-based committees to manage emergency services would also preserve autonomy, making certain that local needs remain a focus while sharing the cost. These solutions highlight how these towns can work together without sacrificing their independence.

Home rule is affirmed in Article IX of New York’s Constitution. Coercing towns into these mergers will only centralize authority and silence residents. Any policy, even those that tout the illusion of government efficiency, that diminishes local autonomy is an attack on liberty.

If you value localized liberty, it’s time to act. Attend your local town board and county legislative meetings to defend self-rule and challenge the centralization of power. Demand open debate and transparency on any proposed plans. Support local organizations, including Libertarian Party of New York affiliates, that continue to stand against unfunded mandates and continue to uphold voluntary cooperation over the ‘efficiency’ of government restructuring. Write letters to local newspaper editors to share your views. Connect with your neighboring towns to build alliances for support. These kinds of actions will empower residents to preserve their local autonomy.

True efficiency does not require sacrificing your liberty. Strengthening communities to innovate, eliminating state mandates, and removing obstacles can reduce costs while still protecting local rule. Voluntary reform is the path to genuine self-government, not an enforced consolidation of services.

articles.title: ICE, Hypocrisy, and the Failure of Both Parties
articles.author: Pietro Geraci
articles.summary: Argues that neither Democrats nor Republicans have solved immigration enforcement problems and that both parties fail on inflation, housing and other costs.

body.text: Democrats are just as responsible for the tragedies in Minneapolis as Trump and his ICE goons.

That sounds absurd until you realize, Dear Reader, that Democrats had an opportunity to abolish ICE during the Biden administration, but instead voted to continue funding the agency. They also had an opportunity to resolve the immigration crisis, disincentivizing illegal immigration by restoring the Ellis Island immigration policy - performing health and criminal checks on prospective immigrants and issuing green cards to those who pass - but instead stuck with the status quo, setting the stage for the current chaos.

Don’t get me wrong, the blatant lying from Trump administration officials about the cold-blooded murders of Renée Good and Alex Pretti, the blind, unquestioning loyalty of Team MAGA to Trump no matter what travesties he unleashes, and the discarding of the First, Second and Fourth Amendments by the political Right are alarming, but Democratic politicians can miss me with their huffing and puffing.

The disturbing truth is that neither party wants to solve the immigration crisis, because both parties can use it for fundraising and campaigning. Just think of all the money Democratic Congressional candidates will raise on this issue, while Republicans will continue to clamor for more ICE activity and fundraise off fear to stop these Democratic candidates. After all, this country must be rid of dangerous law-breakers, like toddlers, Native Americans and college students.
Yes, I am aware that there are dangerous criminals among immigrants, but undocumented immigrants commit fewer crimes than those that came here legally and far fewer than native-born citizens.

ICE is targeting hard-working parents and teenagers; there are even documented cases of U.S. citizens being wrongfully detained due to profiling. How is deporting people who have been here for years, working hard and paying taxes, making America safe or great?

Moreover, why should we continue to trust either party to solve our nation’s most pressing issues? Both fail miserably: on inflation, housing costs, healthcare, education, and foreign policy, we are told year after year to accept less, pay more, and lower our expectations. Why should we continue to trust two parties that repeatedly demonstrate their inability—or unwillingness— to solve the nation’s most pressing problems?

It’s time to cast aside both major parties and put your faith in the Libertarian Party, the only party which stands for all your rights all the time! The LP has a comprehensive plan to fix our immigration policies and is committed to abolishing ICE. The LP’s commitment to free market and classical liberal policies would lead to improvements with the aforementioned issues as well, as demonstrated by Argentina’s Libertarian President Javier Milei.
Stop depending on parties with no incentive to help you! Learn more about the Libertarian Party at lp.org and lpny.org and get involved today!

articles.title: Creating a Free Market in Private Housing and Child Care
articles.author: Vincent O’Neill
articles.summary: Proposes free-market answers to the “affordability crisis”: tax-free rent from one tenant, curb rights, unregulated child care and tripled compensation for eminent domain.

body.text: Everyone keeps hearing about an “Affordability Crisis.” This is no surprise, once you notice how Private Property Rights are constantly being abused.
The solution to the problem of affordability will be found through Free markets and property rights.
Free market solutions are based on common sense and consent.

Government interventionist ‘solutions’ are short-sighted, and are based on coercion and limiting choices. They also require unlimited spending and debt, and are designed to allow issues to be postponed until after next election. Their ‘solutions’ never solve anything.
The following are examples of free market solutions based on property rights and consent.
1. All homeowners will be allowed to rent to one tenant income tax free at the state level.
This will be permitted only in the absence of a restrictive covenant which forbids this, which is common in gated communities.
2. Any income provided from a second or additional tenant will taxable at the state and local level.
A family, consisting of parents and children, counts as one tenant. If grandma moves in, she is a second tenant.
A boyfriend and girlfriend, or roommates, count as one tenant. If an additional person moves in, he is a second tenant.
Property owners can rent or decline to rent to anyone they choose. It is their property.
A “certificate of occupancy” will not be required. A tenant may request one, but the homeowner doesn’t need to comply.
It is also worth noting that Jeffrey Tucker pointed out in one of his books that private homeowners mainly want steady income and a reliable tenant. This keeps costs for the tenant low.
Homeowners therefore have less of a desire for rent increases than public housing officials.
“Curb Rights” are the right of the homeowner to the area immediately in front of his property. He can rent the space to anyone he chooses and for any price.
This option will be available in any area where overnight parking is allowed.
4. Creating a free market in child care. Free market child care vs. government approved child care:
Child Care will consist of 2 choices. These will consist of either a private, unregulated, tax-free market or a taxable and regulated market with government regulations to set rates.
A Private, Unregulated, and Tax Free Market-an example.
Your neighbors raised two fairly well-behaved children who grew up, got jobs, and moved out, and are now willing to provide child care. That is their reference for you.
So as long as you give your consent, they would watch your child and any child care income would be tax free at the state and local level, although they would have to pay national income tax.

So, for example, if they watch 5 children for 40 hours per week for $100 each, they would receive $500 per week, $25,000 per year, tax free, plus two weeks vacation. The parents would be paying $2.50 per hour, $5,200 per year. Child care would primarily consist of allowing the children to play in the yard, watch T.V., or have a book read to them, and eating lunch.
The unregulated private market would also provide many other options.
Government approved and regulated child care, with government rates applying.
New York rates for the Child Care Assistance Program in 2024 (CCAP) varied from $350-$404 weekly per child.
Anyone who wants government involvement in this issue will have to pay the government price and obey its rules.
Additionally, as with private housing, private providers want steady income and have much less of an incentive to raise rates. Private rates are set by the market, government rates by politicians.
Providing compensation for eminent domain and civil forfeiture

Compensation for Eminent Domain seizures will be three times the value of the property. The owner of a property worth $300,000 seized through Eminent Domain will receive $900,000 in compensation. Currently, some homeowners who are targets of seizure through eminent domain end up slightly ahead, some slightly behind, and some are ‘over a barrel’, with their negotiating position destroyed, at which point they are cheated. This will provide compensation.
B. Civil forfeiture is THEFT, and is ended.
All victims will be compensated with $100,000 each, tax-free.
Criminal forfeiture is another matter, and remains unchanged.
The ideas above will provide workable solutions to the government interventionist-created problems of “affordability.”

articles.title: Mark Braiman Nominated for Lt. Governor
articles.author: Andrew Kolstee
articles.summary: The State Committee chose Mark Braiman as the Libertarian candidate for Lieutenant Governor, postponed Attorney General and Comptroller nominations, and elected oversight committee members.

body.text: The Libertarian Party of New York State Committee met on Sunday, March 8, 2026. The main items of business were to nominate candidates for the remaining vacant positions of Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, and Comptroller.

In October 2025, Larry Sharpe was nominated as the Libertarian Party candidate for Governor of New York. Since then, he has been campaigning and continuing his full Sharpe by visiting all 62 counties across the state. He has also entered the race for the Republican nomination in which he needs over 15,000 signatures to primary Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman. He has chosen Lewis County Sheriff Michael Carpinelli as his lieutenant governor candidate in the Republican Party primary race.

At the State Committee meeting, the Libertarian Party of New York met to determine the slate of candidates. There were two candidates nominated for Lieutenant Governor: Mark Braiman and Vincent O’Neill. A third candidate, Lewis County Sheriff Michael Carpinelli, was also nominated. Since Carpinelli is an enrolled member of the Republican Party, the party rules required a two-thirds vote of the State Committee in order to enter Carpinelli into nomination. The State Committee voted 9-4-12 against entering Carpinelli into nomination.
Mark Braiman and Vincent O’Neill spoke on behalf of their candidacies, while Secretary Andrew Kolstee spoke on behalf of None of the Above (NOTA).

In the first round, Braiman and NOTA both received nine votes, while O’Neill received two votes. O’Neill was dropped from the ballot. In the second round, Braiman and NOTA tied once again, each with ten votes. In the third and final round, Mark Braiman was nominated for Lieutenant Governor over NOTA by a vote of 16 to 7.

No candidates were nominated for the positions of Attorney General and Comptroller, and they have been postponed to no later than April 12, 2026, which is the Sunday before the independent petitioning period begins. Interested candidates are asked to contact the party at info@lpny.org.

In addition to nominees, the State Committee elected positions on the Elections Oversight Committee, which will oversee the election of the 2026-2028 LPNY State Committee. Samuel Hordeski, Steven Becker, and Andrew Kolstee were elected to the committee and join Chair Duane Whitmer as members of the committee. After the committee meets, there will be an announcement for anyone interested in running for State Committee to register to be a candidate.

body.text: Here are the latest updates from the Libertarian Party of New York.

The Libertarian Party of New York has opened applications for individuals interested in serving on its State Committee for the 2026-2028 term. The State Committee functions as the governing body of the party in New York, overseeing its direction, operations, and organizational decisions at the state level.

Those wishing to serve are invited to complete registration, which will be reviewed by the Elections Oversight Committee to determine eligibility under party rules. Candidates who meet the requirements will then be submitted to their respective County Affiliates within their Judicial Districts, which are responsible for voting on representatives for each Judicial District.

The deadline to submit applications is April 30, 2026 (unless the State Committee votes to extend; any such action will be announced if voted upon). Individuals considering applying are encouraged to review the party rules in full to understand both the process and the responsibilities involved in serving on the State Committee.

New York has a full slate of Delegates to the 2026 Libertarian National Convention in Grand Rapids, Michigan. We also have several alternates. If you are interested in becoming a Delegate, there may still be an opportunity to become an alternate in the event that Delegate positions open up. Contact info@ lpny.org if you are interested in a Delegate or alternate position.
Save the Date: October 24, 2026 – Mount Kisco, New York.

Plans for the 2026 LPNY State Convention are well underway. Catrina Rocco, Chair of the Conventions Oversight Committee is organizing the event. This will be the gathering where the newly elected 2026– 2028 State Committee convenes to elect the Executive Committee. More details will be announced as the date approaches — stay tuned!

There are still no updates on the Senate bill (S01870) or Assembly bill (A02724), which would reduce the thresholds for independent and third-party ballot access. Both remain in committee. Please contact your State Senator and Assemblymember to express your support for these critical reforms. Every voice matters in advancing fair ballot access for all New Yorkers.

articles.title: The Case for Equalizing All 12 Federal Reserve Banks
articles.author: Rich Purtell
articles.summary: Richard Purtell argues that giving all 12 regional Federal Reserve Banks equal weight would improve representation, transparency, financial stability and public trust.

body.text: Advocates for Federal Reserve reform have long argued that the United States would benefit from equalizing the power, influence, and structural weight of all 12 regional Federal Reserve Banks. While the Federal Reserve System was designed in 1913 to balance regional economic interests, the modern economy looks nothing like the one that existed a century ago. Today, equalizing the Reserve Banks could strengthen democratic accountability, improve monetary policy responsiveness, and create a more resilient financial system.

The first major benefit is greater regional representation in national monetary policy. At present, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York holds unique authority, including permanent voting rights on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) and responsibility for implementing monetary policy operations. Supporters of equalization argue that this structure over weighs the financial interests of one region—Wall Street—at the expense of the broader national economy. Equalizing the Reserve Banks would distribute influence more evenly, ensuring that economic conditions in the Midwest, South, Mountain West, and rural regions carry the same weight as those in New York. In an economy as diverse as the United States, this broader representation could lead to more balanced policy decisions.

A second benefit is increased transparency and accountability. The current system gives some Reserve Banks more visibility and operational authority than others, which can create opacity around decision making. Equalization would standardize governance structures, reduce disparities in institutional power, and make it easier for the public and Congress to understand how decisions are made. When each Reserve Bank operates under the same rules, with comparable responsibilities and influence, oversight becomes clearer and more consistent.

Third, equalization could enhance financial stability. Concentrating operational authority in a single Reserve Bank—particularly one located in the nation’s financial capital— can create systemic vulnerabilities. By distributing responsibilities more evenly across all 12 Banks, the Federal Reserve System could reduce single point of failure risks. A more decentralized operational structure would also allow the Fed to tap into a wider range of regional expertise, improving its ability to detect emerging risks in different parts of the country.

Finally, equalization would strengthen public trust. Many Americans view the Federal Reserve as distant or overly aligned with financial elites. A more balanced structure—one that visibly treats all regions equally—could help rebuild confidence in the institution. When people see their region represented fairly, they are more likely to view the system as legitimate.

In short, equalizing the 12 Federal Reserve Banks offers a path toward a more democratic, transparent, resilient, and modern central banking system—one better suited to the economic realities of today and tomorrow.

articles.title: Three Paths to Ballot Access in New York
articles.author: James Harris
articles.summary: James Harris outlines three ways to gather roughly 60,000 petition signatures: a traveling advocate, grassroots bootstrapping and a lottery-ticket gamble.

body.text: Getting on the New York State ballot requires approximately 60,000 signatures collected in April and May. There are three basic approaches to achieving this goal: Plans A, B, and C.
This is our present approach. We have an advocate traveling across New York State, campaigning alongside Libertarians and others.
He is raising awareness and funds for the campaign. Thank you to Larry Sharpe for taking on this role.
This is the grassroots plan. Most Libertarians reading this can identify one to four registered voters willing to sign our petition in April. The key is to find them now.
Secure their commitment now. Once someone signs, they are far more likely to sign again in future years. Each year, add one or two more.
At each meeting, everyone contributes one dollar and buys a lottery ticket. If we win, we advertise our way onto the ballot or fund an advocate to do it for us.
There are thousands of Libertarians who want to be part of a successful action. This is something we can all take pride in.

articles.title: Petitioning, Ballot Access, and the Road Ahead
articles.author: Andrew Kolstee
articles.summary: Andrew Kolstee explains the party's silence during petitioning, the difficulty of ballot access, a coming campaign, ballot access bills and convention plans.

body.text: You may be wondering why the Libertarian Party of New York has been silent through the petitioning period this year. This was intentional, and once this year’s process is over in early June, we will elaborate on the decision to be silent, and on the decisions of the State Committee.

The ballot access situation in New York remains extremely difficult. The current requirements continue to place a heavy burden on independent and third-party candidates, especially organizations made up primarily of volunteers. These challenges force us to make hard decisions about where to focus our time and resources.

The Executive Committee has discussed several ideas for moving the Libertarian Party of New York in a different direction. We know what has worked, we know what has not worked, and we recognize that continuing to operate the same way is not sustainable under the current system.

We are currently working on a campaign that will be announced shortly. This effort is intended to help move the party forward while recognizing the practical limitations we face as a volunteer organization.

We also want to hear from members. If you have particular ideas, issues, or proposals that you believe the party should discuss, please contact us. This process will not be easy, but we appreciate everyone’s patience as we navigate the next steps.

Plans for the 2026 LPNY State Convention are underway. This will be the gathering where the newly elected 2026-2028 State Committee convenes to elect the Executive Committee. Additional information will be sent out shortly. Save the Date for October 24, 2026 in Mount Kisco, New York.
The June newsletter will also include a recap on the 2026 National Convention.

Please contact your State Senator and Assemblymember to express your support for these critical reforms. Every voice matters in advancing fair ballot access for all New Yorkers.

body.text: This issue is intended to be a shorter update, with a more substantial newsletter planned for July as there will be some substantial updates.

At the convention, New York joined a region with New Jersey, Illinois, and Wisconsin. The region elected its representatives to the Libertarian National Committee, with Representative Tyler Danke of Wisconsin and Alternate Representative Rose Leatherman of New York selected to serve.
We thank all of New York’s delegates who attended the convention and represented the state party.

Once that process is complete, affiliates will vote on State Committee representatives. Affiliates will have until August 31 to complete their voting. Plans are underway for the 2026 LPNY State Convention, which will be held on October 24, 2026, in Mount Kisco, New York. Additional details, including registration information, will be sent out once registration opens. Members should save the date and watch for future announcements.

As noted last month, the ballot access situation in New York remains extremely difficult. The current requirements continue to place a heavy burden on independent and third-party candidates, especially organizations made up primarily of volunteers.

The Executive Committee has continued discussing ways to move the Libertarian Party of New York in a different direction. We know what has worked, we know what has not worked, and we recognize that continuing to operate the same way is not sustainable under the current system.
Plans are being finalized for a campaign effort this year. There are no additional updates to announce yet, but more information will be shared when available.

articles.title: 2026 LPNY Convention
articles.author: Catrina Rocco
articles.summary: Catrina Rocco invites members to the October 24, 2026 LPNY convention at Hotel MTK in Mount Kisco, with speakers, candidate training, roasts, an auction and a plan to run 50 candidates in 2027.

body.text: Dear Fellow Libertarians and Liberty Lovers, You are warmly invited to join us for the Libertarian Party of New York’s 2026 Convention on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at Hotel MTK in Mount Kisco, New York. Check in for the daytime program opens at 9:30 a.m. with business set to start sharply at 10:00 a.m. Our daytime programming includes our LPNY business meeting with lunch being served at noon in the company of our lunchtime speaker Diane Sare. LPNY business is scheduled to conclude at 4:30 p.m. with Jim Ostrowski joining us as our end of business speaker, followed by closing remarks from the Chair.
The evening program will feature a special Candidate Training Breakout Session and dinner with our keynote speaker, Eric Brakey.

Eric Brakey is a former Maine State Senator and current Executive Director of the Free State Project. Eric will share critical lessons and practical takeaways from his book, The Liberty Candidate’s Practical Guide to Door Knocking.

This training is especially important as the Libertarian Party of New York announces its plan to run 50 Libertarian candidates for local offices across the state in 2027. County Affiliates, We Need You!
Then, It’s Time for Liberty After Dark!

Following dinner and candidate training, we’ll keep the energy going during our Liberty After Dark party that will feature a candidate meet and greet to introduce you to candidates endorsed by local county affiliates. Brett Yarris, running for Putnam County Executive, will be attending.

Afterwards, you can take the mic and roast a Libertarian. Have something you’ve always wanted to say about your fellow Libertarians? This is your chance to take the microphone and let it fly! Check out the Liberty’s Elite Sponsor package about how to make it to the top of the roast line up. Roasts will continue throughout the evening after every three or four songs played. Your Liberty After Dark Ticket also includes an evening full of sweet treats, cash bar and access to our table auction so you can bid on unique items and experiences while supporting the Libertarian Party of New York.

Please visit lpny. org/2026-lpny-convention to reserve your package and stay. Discounted rooms are available now thru September 23, and reduced priced packages are on sale until August 31. We look forward to seeing you!

articles.title: A Call to Action to County Affiliates
articles.author: Catrina Rocco
articles.summary: Catrina Rocco asks county affiliates to meet their state legislators about a minor-party nominating petition and return reports by October 3, 2026.

body.text: We can’t assume that many of our state legislators are fully aware or have a clear understanding of the grievances and concerns of libertarians in New York State. But we can safely assume that our elected officials will continue to remain in the dark or happily discount the cruciality of matters that we proclaim are important to us until we are willing to make it our duty to engage in regular contact with our elected officials via face-to-face conversations, phone calls, and letter-writing campaigns to their district offices.

This past winter the Libertarian Party of New York asked its affiliates to take part in a call to action. We urgently asked our affiliates to get involved by reaching out to their local state legislators to voice their concerns about matters such as ballot access rules, qualified immunity, the prevention of a mandatory adult vaccine database, and allowing homeschooled children to participate in district sports. However, we received only a handful of returned reports this time around.

The LPNY has extended its deadline to October 3, 2026 to provide more time for county affiliates to engage with their elected state representatives and to return their reports to us. We hope that members of each county affiliate will take the time to visit, write, call or email their state assembly members and senators about these issues and mention any additional concerns that are relevant to them.

At this time we encourage you to emphasize the need for a minor-party nominating petition. In 39 states there is a clearer distinction between the “independent” and “minor party” concepts and after what we are seeing in Putnam County where the County Executive failed to secure an endorsement from the local affiliate and yet is running on a ballot line named libertarian (with our torch!) we need this more than ever. Let’s take the appropriate small steps toward regaining our ballot access. You’re encouraged to discuss the issue,- but not bombard -your legislators for a signature requirement change. The first step is to secure a minor party nominating petition that is distinctly ours. Recognition is key.

Please refer to the Quick Guide to Meeting with Your State Legislators for brief talking points and a list of district office addresses and phone numbers. If you need another copy, don’t hesitate to email crocco@ lpny.org for one.

We thank you for contributing your valuable time to support this very important endeavor. As county leaders and active libertarians, you are the backbone of the Libertarian Party and your efforts continually kindle the flame of liberty!
Kindly return the accompanying form to the LPNY by email to the individuals listed below by Saturday, October 3, 2026.
Rich Purtell. Legislative Affairs Director rpurtell@lpny.org

articles.title: Election Integrity
articles.author: Vincent O’Neill
articles.summary: Vincent O'Neill lays out a reform agenda: end taxpayer-funded primaries, equalize ballot access, expand debates, require photo ID, restrict absentee voting and change legislative procedure and campaign finance.

body.text: “There is a way of asking us for our reasons that leads us not only to forget our best reasons but also to conceive a stubborn aversion to all reasons. This way of asking makes people very stupid and is a trick used by tyrannical people.” - Friedrich Nietzsche, “The Gay Science,” P. 208. Note: “The Gay Science” is Philosophy.
A comprehensive approach must be used to provide an outline for honest government, and it follows.
A process must be in place for peaceful, orderly, and honest elections, as well as the transfer of power. The process should be simple, and should not resemble World War II.
The following are a few requirements.
All advantages Republicans and Democrats have given themselves against potential Competition will be ended.
Political parties are private entities, not the ‘government’, and must select their candidates privately in whatever manner they choose, at their own expense.

Ending taxpayer-funded primaries will create an interesting situation. Will private political parties allow ‘absentee ballots,’ ‘early voting,’ and ‘mail-in voting,” or recognize their obvious enabling of dishonest elections? Would the Democrats retain the concept of “super-delegates’ and weighted voting?
B. All ‘ballot access’ requirements must be the same for all political parties and individuals.
They also must be reduced tremendously and quickly. Some are state, some are national, but the same procedure should apply. Reduce all requirements by 50%, 3 years in a row.

An alternative would be to require all independent candidates for an office to file nominating petitions with the names of 1,000 registered voters, acquired over the two months from May 1 to July 1, in order to qualify for ballot status.
Registered voters would be allowed to sign for more than one candidate.
Individual political parties could then set their own rules for nominating a candidate.

Public debate on issues should be expanded, not limited. The actions of the Republicans and the Democrats have been reprehensible. Their primary version of public policy communication consists of outright lies and the occasional resort to slander. A logical conclusion is that they have nothing worthwhile to offer on any policy issue and are afraid of any competition.
All incumbents must offer to debate their challengers. There must be at least one public debate among them in the month preceding the vote provided their challenger’s accept.
Unless the challenger(s) refuse to debate, failure to do so will result in the elimination of that party’s candidate for that office until the next election.

Everyone satisfying ballot access requirements will be eligible to be included in state and local debates. Presidential debates will include all candidates eligible to receive enough Electoral Votes to win the presidency will be included. A candidates’ “standing in the polls” is irrelevant.

The reliance on ‘polls’ displays the shallow level of public debate in this country. You can get any result you want from a poll, depending on how you frame the question. (Also, most people refuse to respond.)
D. The Electoral College and State’s Rights must be preserved. This is also important for honest elections.

“Sixteen years ago, in 2005, the Carter-Baker Commission on Federal Election Reform issued a report that proposed a uniform system of requiring a photo ID in order to vote in U.S. elections. The report also pointed out that widespread absentee voting makes fraud more likely. Voter files contain ineligible, duplicate, fictional, and deceased voters, a fact more easily exploited using absentee voters to commit fraud. Citizens who vote absentee are more susceptible to pressure and intimidation. And vote-buying schemes are far easier when citizens vote by mail. The committee’s two ranking members were former President Jimmy Carter, a Democrat, and former Secretary of State James Baker III, a Republican.” - John R. Lott, “Is Ensuring Election Integrity Anti-Democratic”, Imprimis, October 2021, p.1
That common sense outlook has now been turned on its head. The political establishment has been working hard to create DISHONEST ELECTIONS. Their actions must be countered.
A Picture ID should be necessary to vote.
For example, a picture ID is currently necessary to purchase the allergy pill Claritin. (purchases are also limited to a maximum of 15 at a time). Displaying a picture ID takes no time at all.
The vote would occur on one day only.
The only citizens entitled to an absentee ballot should be active duty military personnel.
If someone wants to spend November in Florida but vote in New York, they will have to return to New York to do so.

“It wasn’t just Brooklyn voters who received absentee envelopes with the wrong name and address on them-hundreds of voters on Long Island were affected as well. Now New York has to resend more than 100,000 ballots before the election.” - New York Post, Page 1, October 1, 2020.
F. Cleaning Voter Rolls and addressing Mail-in Voting

Judicial Watch has been actively doing both. The August, 2020 “Verdict”, among other months of this publication, details much that they have done, including suing California Governor Gavin Newsom for violating the State Constitution.

The January, 2021 issue of “The Verdict” reported that Judicial Watch found 353 counties in 29 states with Voter Registration Rates over 100%. Fourteen other states either don’t post voter registration data online at all or don’t post enough information to determine registration rates compared to the general population.

Districts should be based on easily recognized geography. Population density is a secondary consideration. Party registration should not figure in the process at all. The Motor Voter laws can stay, as long as no party registration occurs at the same time. The concept of government agencies collecting party registration information must end. Registering with a political party, or no political party at all, must become a purely private decision.
Once this has been done successfully, there will rarely be a need to re-draw districts unless there is a major earthquake, or if part of the earth falls into the sea.
The starting point will be the current districts.
2. Procedural Changes for Operation of a Government
A comprehensive approach to problems from a free market perspective will go a long way to countering this. Addressing elected officials and voting on issues once elected.

You recall the absurd number of times and number of co-sponsors Ron Paul needed to bring End the Fed and related issues to a discussion and votes. This type of thing happens all the time, and it happens at the national and state level. A few suggestions follow to change this:
A. Any item brought up by a member must be discussed and voted on in the current session, within reason.
B. Exactly One co-sponsor will be required to bring this about.

C. Members can only vote on an issue if they certify, under penalty of perjury, that they have read the bill in its entirety before casting their vote. A member can vote ‘present’ if they haven’t read the bill in its entirety.
They can also ask for a one week postponement votes.
Any member will be able to simply ask to postpone a vote for a reasonable time to allow more discussion. One week, for example.
The focus should be on addressing issues, not avoiding them.
Incumbents will only be permitted to raise money for one year before a vote for re-election will occur. Currently, they raise money every day of the year.

Any money left over after the election must be dispersed. This can be given to anyone they see fit to disperse it to, with the exception of members of their family. Dispersal will not count as a charitable contribution.
Any individual will be permitted to donate any amount of money to any candidate they choose.

Keep in mind that the major political reform to come out of Watergate was to create campaign finance restrictions in order to make sure that a Eugene McCarthy would never again be allowed to challenge the establishment candidate.
The hindering of ballot access is the largest problem in the political process, and it must be addressed.
The proper and necessary response is to call for a boycott of all Republican and Democrat candidates, at least until or unless ballot access problems are properly addressed.
After that, it is unlikely that anyone will be able to find any reason to vote for one of their candidates. Meanwhile, the Libertarian Party will be addressing issues in detail.
The Republicans and Democrats have nothing positive to offer. The country is $40 trillion in debt, a number that is expanding by $2 trillion plus per year. They have no plans to address this issue.
The U.S. has bombed 32 countries without a declaration of war since the end of World War II. This is more than one-third of the people on Earth.

And World War II, it should be pointed out, ended when the United States government committed the biggest war crime in the history of the universe, the dropping of atomic bombs on the Japanese civilian centers of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. No one has ever been held accountable for this atrocity.

articles.title: State Committee Elected
articles.subtitle: 2026-28 Term Begins October 24
articles.author: Andrew Kolstee
articles.summary: Sixteen members were elected to the 2026-2028 State Committee across seven judicial districts, with many vacancies; the new committee takes office October 24.

body.text: The Libertarian Party of New York has completed its elections for the 2026-2028 State Committee, with 16 members elected across seven Judicial Districts, and numerous vacancies. The results were certified by the Elections Oversight Committee on September 28, 2026. The newly elected State Committee will take office and convene for the first time at the LPNY State Convention on October 24, 2026, in Mount Kisco.

The State Committee serves as the governing body of the Libertarian Party of New York, overseeing the direction, operations, and organizational decisions of the state party. Members are elected by County Affiliates within New York’s Judicial Districts.

Preparations for the 2026–2028 State Committee elections began at the March 8, 2026 State Committee meeting with the election of the Elections Oversight Committee. Andrew Kolstee served as Chair of the committee and was joined by Steven Becker, Samuel Hordeski, and Duane Whitmer. Later, Justin Carman and Catrina Rocco were elected to two of the vacancies on the committee.

Following the formation of the committee, applications were opened to Libertarian Party members interested in serving on the State Committee. Registrants were reviewed by the Elections Oversight Committee to determine their eligibility under party rules. Eligible candidates were then submitted to the Local Affiliates located within their respective Judicial Districts for voting.

The registration period was ultimately extended through July 5, 2026. Following the Elections Oversight Committee’s review of the registrants, candidates were certified on July 8 and voting by the Local Affiliates began. Affiliates were given through August 31 to complete their voting.
After the affiliate voting process was completed and the results reviewed, the Elections Oversight Committee certified the elected members on September 28.
The following members were elected to the 2026–2028 State Committee:

Judicial District 13 (no elections held - 1 vacancy) Of the 16 elected, 13 are incumbents and 3 are new: Theresa Corrigan (Monroe County Secretary), Nicholas Castellano (Westchester-Putnam Secretary), and Nicole Hewson (Orange County Vice Chair).
No State Committee members were elected from Judicial Districts 1, 2, 4, 10, 12, or 13. Judicial District 12 had no candidates.

Other candidates appearing in the final district voting included Chance Haywood in Judicial District 1; Paul Grindle in Judicial District 2; Evan Lebrecht in Judicial District 3; Charles Williams in Judicial District 4; Richard Purtell in Judicial District 6; Michael Cody in Judicial District 8; Chuck Monsanto and Daniel Donnelly in Judicial District 9; Jonathan Gunther, Christian Padgett, Raymond Negron, Vincent O’Neill, Robert Schuon, and Blay Tarnoff in Judicial District 10; and Susan Overeem-Cummings in Judicial District 13.

Both Nassau and Suffolk Counties held elections, but after the August 30 deadline. Both elected four candidates as their representatives, but it will be up to the State Committee to determine how they fill the vacancies. Those candidates are: Jonathan Gunther, Christian Padgett, Robert Schuon, and Blay Tarnoff.
The members elected for the 2026– 2028 term will officially take office on October 24, 2026, when the new State Committee convenes during the LPNY State Convention at Hotel MTK in Mount Kisco.
One of the first responsibilities of the newly constituted State Committee will be the election of the LPNY Executive Committee for the coming term.

The October 24 meeting will mark the transition from the 2024-2026 State Committee to the 2026-2028 State Committee and begin the next two-year organizational term for the Libertarian Party of New York.

articles.title: Blay Tarnoff Launches Campaign for Congress
articles.author: Tarnoff for Congress Campaign
articles.summary: Libertarian Blay Tarnoff, on the November 3 ballot in NY District 4 in southern Nassau County, campaigns against socialism and for a federal Civil Rights Bureau.

body.text: NASSAU COUNTY, NY – September 14, 2026 – Blay Tarnoff will be on the ballot as the Libertarian Candidate for Congress in NY District 4, which encompasses southern Nassau County, in the General Election to be held this November 3, 2026.

Blay understands that major segments of society have legitimate grievances against the current system, which are caused by socialist policy at every level of government. His central message is that socialism is unconstitutional, and he promises to spearhead legislation to END it.

“I will introduce legislation to enable anyone suffering under socialist policy at the state level to bring their case to a federal Civil Rights Bureau to bring suit on their behalf. At the federal level, I will put forward legislation to privatize all the necessary functions of the federal administrative agencies and then abolish them. I will also end inflation by pegging the dollar to gold or bitcoin.”

“Every socialist measure helps a few people while hurting many, many more. After decades of creeping socialism, things are now so bad people are desperate for drastic change. They blame the system. They are right. But, the answer is not to abandon freedom, it is to double down on it.”

Socialism violates the Contract and Republican Form of Government clauses of the Constitution, as well as various clauses of the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments, in addition to the Ninth and Tenth. Socialism is a violent attack on Civil Rights. Blay would expand or create legislation parallel to 42 USC §1983, the act that empowers citizens to fight violations of their Civil Rights, and a Civil Rights Bureau to empower citizens to enforce it.

Blay would also reform the education and health care systems, making them the envy of the world. He would protect the environment, the right to run your business and profession without government harassment, interference or competition, and restore and protect the right and means to defend yourself, your family, your community and your country. He would also phase out all foreign aid and subsidies. “I would restore your right to pursue happiness in any manner you see fit, so long as you do not violate the rights of others.” He would give people a reason once again to be proud of their government and to make them eager and proud to protect and defend it.

“Wealth is freedom. Handouts make people dependent and helpless. The best job security is knowing you can find another job in five minutes. The best housing security is to be able to afford many places to live. The best medical security is the availability of excellent, reasonably priced care and the ability to pay for it. Politicians do not support these policies because free, independent people do not need politicians. Politicians are also reluctant to go too far in eliminating an ideology which brings the people in government more wealth and power. The answer is not to run to the politicians for help and handouts, it is to be free and independent enough not to need them.”

Blay will attack not only the virulent socialism currently infesting the Democrat Party, but all socialism. “’Moderate’ Democrats have advocated incremental socialism as ‘social justice’ for decades, and are now crying crocodile tears that ‘extremists’ are proliferating in their party. But, it was always inevitable that a tiny amount of cancer would eventually metastasize into full-blown disease. Republicans talk a good game, but rarely carry their words forward. The socialist parasite may be a bug, but the creeping misery it causes is a feature. After they bleed the host society financially, they blame it for the predictable misery. Then, they promise the socialist utopia of love and plenty will fix all the problems they created. Once they lie their way into power, though, they step up the misery because people who are poor, weak and dependent are easy to control.”

Everyone cannot live at the expense of everyone else. Socialism poses an existential threat to freedom and is completely incompatible with the principles upon which this nation was founded. It can and must be ended.

Blay Tarnoff has been a Libertarian activist and representative since 1990. He is currently County Chair of the Nassau County Libertarian Party and immediate past Chair of the Libertarian National Judicial Committee. He has spent his career as a computer systems analyst, most recently as technical support for quantitative financial analysts on Wall Street and neural network system developer and presenter at nVidia GPU Technology Conferences. He holds a J.D. from Pace University and an A.B. in mathematics from Brown University.

articles.title: NY Libertarians Urge Voters to Write-In None of the Above for Governor, Reject Hochul and Blakeman
articles.summary: LPNY's VOTE NOTA campaign urges New Yorkers to write in None of the Above for governor, protesting a two-candidate ballot and restrictive ballot-access laws.

body.text: ALBANY, N.Y. — For the second consecutive gubernatorial election, New York voters will face a general election ballot featuring only two candidates for governor, despite five political party lines. In response, the Libertarian Party of New York is calling for a statewide “None of the Above” (VOTE NOTA) write-in protest in the November 3 election, challenging both the lack of competition and the state’s restrictive ballot-access laws.

Gov. Kathy Hochul appears on the Democratic and Working Families lines, while Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman appears on the Republican, Conservative, and Vote Affordable lines. Neither faced a contested gubernatorial primary, leaving voters in both major parties without an opportunity to choose between competing nominees.

Through its VOTE NOTA campaign, the party is urging New Yorkers dissatisfied with both candidates to use the gubernatorial write-in space to express that dissatisfaction rather than support either major-party nominee or stay home. LPNY describes the effort as a protest against a system in which five ballot lines offer only two choices, with the aim of demonstrating opposition to the political status quo and reducing the share of voter support received by the two major-party candidates.

“New Yorkers deserve to choose a governor, not settle for whoever survives the barriers to getting on the ballot,” said Duane Whitmer, Chair of the Libertarian Party of New York. “If no one on that ballot cares about you, no one supports you, and no one deserves your vote, you should be able to say so. That’s what our NOTA campaign is about. Politicians aren’t entitled to your support. They should have to earn it.”

In 2018, the Libertarian Party of New York earned official ballot access for the first time, only to lose it after lawmakers changed election rules in the 2020 state budget, requiring 45,000 petition signatures to place a candidate on the ballot and the greater of 130,000 votes or 2 percent to maintain party status. The new thresholds effectively shut out emerging political parties. But while Albany can keep alternatives off the printed ballot, it cannot prevent New Yorkers from expressing their rejection of both candidates through a write-in vote.

“We are done playing a game whose rules were rewritten to make sure we lose before the first vote is cast,” Skelly said. “If Albany wants a two-party state, it can have one, and it can own the turnout, the cynicism, and the legitimacy crisis that comes with it. We will not staff their stage.”

The LPNY also advocates ballot-access reform through Senate bill S01870 and Assembly bill A02724, which would restore pre-2020 thresholds of 15,000 petition signatures to appear on the ballot and 50,000 votes to qualify for party status, opening the door to greater political competition and more choices for New Yorkers.
